title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference 9.25.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: How do you feel Isaiah did in his first action of the season? >> I did some good stuff, you know. Um obviously it's it's it's such a small sample size and basically played, you know, one half of football, you know, so but uh what we're asking him to do, I thought he got better and better as the as the week went on. Um you know, did some good stuff on Sunday. Certainly like every other position, things to clean up and um but I thought he's attacked it this week. I I like the trajectory, I guess you could say that he's on. >> With with the uh with Garrett being off pop the last few weeks, what have you seen from his progression and just how close is he to return? >> Yeah, um we'll we'll see what uh Sunday has in store, but uh no, he's um he's he's gotten better every week, you know, and he's a guy that I think I've spoken to you, if I haven't, here it is. I'll I'll repeat myself. Like I having to go against him, I had a lot of respect for him as a player. You could just tell he uh he knew what was going on, very talented. Uh and again, when we played him in '24, I was like, "Man, they got another one back there." You know, it we kind of went I took a trip down memory lane today in the team meeting, 2017 through '20. Um Kendrick Bourne, Budda Baker, stuff like that. And uh you know, then you just look at some of the names that were back there with Patrick Peterson and stuff. And and so when Garrett gets there, I'm not saying he's you know, Hall but you know what I mean, like it's just another good football player. And um so uh like where his uh where he's trending, we'll see what Sunday has in store. >> Who do you weigh when you are looking at whether to play Gay or [snorts] Isaiah? >> Yeah, we're just like we do everything else. Who who do who we think's going to give us the best chance to win a football game, you know? And uh good thing about those two is I think both of them can play really good football and give us good chances to win football games. So, um you know, never going to apologize for feeling good about, you know, some of the guys that are out there. Um so, that's what we're looking for. >> How's Roy doing and did you expect him to play this weekend? >> Uh Roy's doing good. Um uh you know, we'll see on Sunday. >> When you're looking at short yardage rushing situations, third and one, fourth and one, is there any different Is there anything different that the offensive line needs to do to be successful in those situations compared to a neutral down, you know, first and 10, whatever? Like, are there different techniques or things they have to do? >> I mean, they have to execute the technique of the play called. Um situationally, uh obviously a defensive call can be different um situationally. Um you know, the defense might have um kind of a different mindset, not in terms of stop them, like no crap, that's like elementary, but like in terms of how their linebackers might fit and stuff like that. Um so, uh there's a lot of different uh angles you could go with short yards. I'm not going to go any further in that. Again, you and I can talk in February. >> Yesterday, Hackett was saying um he thinks it takes about three years for a quarterback to truly understand everything about an offense. And he's like, we're only two weeks into this offense really playing it at full speed. How long do you expect it to take until you guys are fully comfortable running what you're doing? >> Hopefully by the end of this practice. You know, I mean, it's it's I I and I hear I mean, that's that's that'd be perfect. That's that is the uh I love Hackett and and he's not wrong. I mean, and and it's just an opinion, like who like who really really knows that answer. But he has been around a lot a long time. He has coached some really good quarterbacks. He's been around uh with his father coaching really good quarterbacks, Hall of Famers. So, I mean, that's that's a good general synopsis, I guess you could say, of of that. Yeah, three years, that's great and that worked in in in Green Bay, you know, and it's and and has worked in Green Bay very well. Um the reality of the situation is uh nobody has three years. Um I I feel like we have three minutes. Um that's the way I wake up and um you know, now with that being said, if we don't get the result that that that we want, it's like, okay, go back and figure out why. Um I'm not a result-based guy. Um I'm a process-based guy. Uh you know, and uh sometimes you're going to win, sometimes you're going to lose, but if we're, you know, sitting there and say, "Hey, we did everything we could. We were sharp, we were tough, we were together, we played with the right operation, we played with the right play style, and we don't get the score that we want." Man, it sucks in the moment, but again, process over results, you know? And so, I kind of went on a tangent right there, but that's kind of how I feel about all these guys. Like, hey, the urgency to continue to get better, whether it's a quarterback within our system or or the left tackle or the the backup right guard, you know, we all got to have that same sense of urgency. >> You [snorts] have addressed it actually a few times here about talking about why to get ready for this game, but I'm wondering when you were coaching with San Francisco, how much did you feel like the sun beating down on that visiting sideline might have helped you guys? >> It was hot over there. Cuz even and the only reason I know that is um uh and I don't know if it's changed, but I know my wife, when I was on the receiver coach, she was on that side, and so she would get beaten down on it. So, yeah, that's um you know, good thing we're in the desert, right? >> Coaches in general, just, you know, coming off the first loss this week, how do you feel like your guys have just handled this week knowing there's still one more practice today, just kind of reshaping your focus? >> I think they're in a good spot. Think they rolled up their sleeves and got right back to work, you know? Again, process over results. No one and not to be confused with we don't want to win football, you know, that's not what we're saying. I mean, it it sucks on a Sunday and it can sometimes suck on a Monday and sting, and then you have you know, you have cold, hard truth, and that's the way we're going to do stuff around here. You know, we're going to speak truth, and it starts with coaching, you know? Like, if I can't say, "Hey, this is what I did wrong," then then who am I? You know, and but when we get to Wednesday, you move on, you learn, you correct, you move on, you get the game plan in, you roll up your sleeves, you go right back to work, and I thought that's what those guys have done, and you know, again, we're we'll keep preaching it every single Monday going into the next week, no matter what this result may be on Sunday. >> Throughout your entire career, when teams start to feel comfortable in an offense, do you Is it a slow build-up? Like, can you see them getting there, or is it something or maybe both when it just kind of clicks for them? >> I think each year, each game, each team, each everything's a little bit different. It's I I have used the word organic, like organically it does happen, like you're you're always in search for the identity, but if you if you overly push the identity, there's going to be foundational aspects, but like you know, what are what we're going to look like I would say 15 games from now and what we look like now, good or bad, is going to it's going to be different. I just go back to my most recent in the last 3 years. The way we started, I mean, one, we results-based, we were 3 and 6 in 2023 in LA, we were 1 and 4 in in 24, and then last year, you know, we were kind of lingering a little bit and then and then got hot. Actually got hot in basically all 3 years. But the offense was I don't want to say drastically different, but it it definitely evolved and changed as we went, you know, and what we hung our hat on in 23 was so different than what we had hung our hat on in 25. 24, we weren't even really a very good offense. We had spurts of it, but we were very inconsistent, and when we were inconsistent, our defense played really well. And then we kind of got rolling there in the playoffs, you know. So, again, it's like it's when you live in the moment and you just try to put these guys in position to be the best they can be, and again, you you know, you hey, this is what the defense does, this is what we do well, how can we provide the clarity, how can we provide the clarity so these guys can go out and play with the right play style each and every week, and then you take it as it is each and every week. >> What makes the 49ers' 21 personnel package so difficult to stop? >> Um well, I mean, you you think about kind of what I was just saying. I mean, then you date back to uh signing Juice in 2017. It was 10 years ago. And he wasn't a rookie. And drafting George Kittle in in 2017, you know? And so, now he's 10 years in just like Buddha. Um, and Kendrick Bourne. Um, uh Trent's been there since COVID. Uh Kyle's been there for 10 years. Got a quarterback that's been there quite some time now. Uh getting in the right place and all that. So, um there's a lot of factors. I I I could go on and on and on about, you know, one guy or the other. Um, uh I won't even go further, but but those those guys know uh what makes it go. Um, you know, but more more importantly than all that, it's a standard of of of play style. Uh so, even if they're not um I would say maybe perfectly fundamentally, maybe they're not in the perfect play, they can overcome it uh with with play style and and playing fast and playing together. Um, so, you know, it's going to be a difficult task, but um you know, I like where our guys are at. >> Kind of kind of related, but but not just against that look. What what do you guys have to do better in your play action defense than you did last week? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, I mean, just like uh anyone from a defense perspective, you try to get your tails run past. Some teams have them, some teams don't. Not going to say if the Niners have them um because you cuz well, when you hang your hat on that too much, sometimes you can get burned too. But play your keys, play fundamentally sound. When the ball's uh thrown over the middle, go contest it. When it's checked down, rally to the ball. They're going to get their completions. Um how can you eliminate kind of those leaky yardages uh leaky yards? And um you know, that the YAC that they've um they've always been really good at. >> Mike, when you look at McCaffrey and just what he's done and for how long he's done it, just how impressed are you? And what type of challenge is this >> Yeah, he's a stud. And you go back to 2017, the first year we were there and him being drafted in the top 10 and uh having those discussions whether whether we should have taken him at two, we traded back to three and didn't take him, but it was it was uh just a matter of time before Kyle and John were going to get their hands on them and um you know I don't know the numbers back you know like at top of my head. I do remember seeing a stat like two years ago since he's been there and then when he's played and when he hasn't and it's pretty pretty eye-popping if you will. He's he's been a big key as to their success but not to when he hasn't been in there they they still found ways. So you know just another really talented piece of the puzzle in my opinion a future Hall of Fame Hall of Famer. >> Marv, do you have plays specifically designed for him in the in the playbook? >> Yeah yeah I mean you have plays designed for all these guys based on what you feel like they can do best. The thing about the guys that are actually catching the football is you know they're in command and out of control. All he can do and all the other eligibles can do is what their assignment is and then the dictate or the defense will dictate whether that ball gets there or will dictate you know based on our protections and all those kind of things. So you know there's there's definitely certain things that that we do with Marv that we're not doing with other guys. That I won't go into the the nitty-gritty with it but yeah I mean that's that's all these guys. >> You talked about play action defensively on the defensive side of the ball. But this summer you guys were pretty adamant about wanting to look the same on offense by doing that is a lot of play action trying to marry the run and the pass together. I think you guys were 31st in play action usage the first two weeks. Is that something you're cognizant of? Is that something you'd like to do more and I guess what needs to happen? >> It's it's a good question you know we're two weeks in you know and and so um think about the Chargers not as much. Seattle we actually had quite a bit but we just didn't have a lot of plays. You know percentage-wise in the Seattle game I think we called six out of the 40 whatever plays we had which is a a decent amount. So you know and then if I go even further in terms of what it looks like in week three now I'm telling Rod Kyle and all those guys over there you know. So we might have zero we might have 40, I don't know. >> Coach, thanks. >> It's all good. >> Thanks, coach.

Um a cast of guys stepping in in some different roles which I'm sure we'll get to here in a second. But um some great opportunities for guys that that we know um that we trust that are here for a reason. And so um as we continue to evaluate, you know, this week and uh try to get some guys back out there, you know, these first four games, this is that window of the season where guys are getting acclimated to handling week to week coming back, recovering, doing those things. And um you know, certainly a 70 plus game for our defense against the Bears and then coming back with a a dominant performance last week. We've been playing a lot of ball. So, um, you know, we're just going to take him one day at a time and, uh, see if we can get him back out there. >> With Jonathan, I know Monday you were hoping to get more information. Can you bring us up to speed on how we got to this point? Yeah, it was a pretty significant groin injury and um you know, we got multiple opinions about what's the best course of action and uh Jonathan's going to have surgery to to repair the injury and the timeline of return with surgical or non-surgical was going to be similar and um so they were able to get in there and get a bunch of imaging um just in that whole area to kind of see what it's like and um and everybody just put their heads together and agreed this would be the best course of action so we can get them back um and get them rolling again. getting him back and turning similar timelines. This sounds like more than a four game thing to >> Yeah. And that's and that's the reason for the IR is just to make sure that in that process and that time that you know we can we can make some other you know roster decisions um using different guys to help us. >> Dave, you've had Trey Tyson in here for two years. Where where is he at in your mind as far as being roster ready on game day? >> Yeah, Trey is doing a great job for us. the one thing that he showed us um over the course of time was his ability to, you know, help out in the special teams world. Um not just to run the ball, but as a kick returner, as a coverage player, those different types of things. You know, these are these are things that um are a big part of the reason why Trey's still here and a part of our developmental process. So, um I'm excited for Trey. He'll get an opportunity this week to come help us in in one way, shape, or form. >> What is the timeline for for Brooks? Uh I believe the I believe the window was like six to eight weeks. Um I don't know exactly. Um but they just kind of gave us a general window. Some guys faster, some guys a little bit longer. We'll see uh once we have you know once the surgery happens and we'll see how his uh progress goes on the rehab. >> That original groin injury for him was that kind of a was it an overuse thing while Chuba was out during the summer? >> I don't know that. maybe um you know, maybe it was just something structurally that he's still figuring out in his body. Um but it it surfaced again, you know, um without taking the the majority of the carries. So um when things start to present like that, that's where we take all the information, you know, from the past month or so that we've had um and try to make the best decision for JB. >> To clarify, when you say he's going to get his opportunity this week, will he play this week? >> Yeah, Trey will be playing this week. >> Where are you at overall then with the return game with Trey having returned a lot during the preseason? you brought in air who was with you guys back in 2024 camp. Where are you guys at as far as that goes? I know you said Jaylen on Monday someone you'd like to keep back at punt return. So I just >> I'd rather not say just from a game plan standpoint. Um but but bringing guys bringing guys back like air a huge part of that, right? And and you know Jaylen was able to make some noise with the ball in his hands back there. We're also really counting on him counting on him on the offensive side and um has played really well over the last couple weeks. So we just have to make sure that we have options, you know. Um, we had, uh, Austin Eckler come in, you know, and and be able to meet him and and, uh, you know, kind of see where he's at. Another guy who's got return in his past. U, you know, a solid pro. So, uh, and then, of course, Trevor. Trevor's kind of getting closer and closer to that window. We can get him back. So, in the in the meantime, Dan's done a great job of just kind of evaluating the the, you know, totality of guys that we have available for returns to give us some options. >> You anticipate. >> How did how did Jonathan take the news? It just it felt like he was ramping up. for, you know, to sort of get more involved this season. >> Yeah, he was bummed. Um, you know, this hit him hard and, uh, particularly, you know, when it happened after the game, you know, and the guys could feel it, too. And we were just trying to encourage him, you know, this is a part of this process as your body figures out how you're going to go forward, you know, in this new mode. um this is a part of it, you know, and and just being able to share with him, you know, there's um the different experiences that I've had and and the different experiences he's had, you know, these opportunities and my my encouragement to him was God's plan. He knew what was going to happen before it happened for us to just be able to say, "Okay, this is just my next step. This is the new challenge that I have in front of me to attack." And he'll attack it the right way. >> Worked out. Did you work out anybody else? And Do you think Austin will sign here or? >> Uh, I I'm not sure about that. We We just worked out Austin today. >> Dave, is Jaylen Coker kind of dealing with what he was dealing with last week with the ankle? Would you kind of anticipate his path for Sunday being the same or is this a little bit >> very similar? Yeah, we got to be smart about his week and the accumulation. Um, he was able to turn it around pretty quickly last week and and get himself out there. But once you go out there and play another full game, we have to just continue to kind of get him get him going little by little through the week so he can get those reps. >> And on the Browns, it doesn't seem like they've run the ball like a typical Monet offense through two weeks, but is that still a real big part of the emphasis on defense this week? >> Absolutely. And um I know that's what Todd wants to do. I know that he wants to be able to establish that that mentality. Um and it also just opens up the play action passes and the different things that I've seen him do over the course of years. So, um, that's what we're expecting and we're preparing that >> You're also a guy that likes run pass balance. It hasn't been a ton of that so far early on. Are you concerned with this Brooks injury that you might even get a little further away from that balance? >> My concern more is that we're able to block our runs properly, the the running backs get on course and run physically and all that when it shows up. We still have a ways to go to get the run game to where we're all satisfied with it, coaches and players alike. We know what it can look like when we have that balanced attack. On the other side of it, Brad's task is to make yards and score points. He's doing that. So, again, we always want to be able to run the ball. I believe that's what ties our whole the whole style and attitude of our team together. Um, but with that, what's more important is that we're moving the chains, that we're making plays, um, and that we're taking care of the ball. Um, at the end of the day, whatever we got to do to win and so, um, the the offense has found a way to continue to find yards and points. Dave, >> the Browns defense has a lot of young talent. What kind of stands out about those guys when you watch them? >> Yeah, biggest thing jumps off of film is this is a really fast group. Um, you know, you talk about the front, Mason Graham, um, obviously, uh, Jared Verse on the other side and then Carson Swessinger right in the middle. Um, this is a team that's they're a little bit lighter, they're fast, they're really active, they chase the entire group, they play hard, they're striking at the ball. Um, they have a real cool style about how they're playing football. And again, when things pop out and maybe they don't cover a concept well here and there, I know that's a communication thing as as groups go through those uh those growing pains of playing football together, but um this is a group that I really respect and um was able to talk about them a little bit today in the meeting and and really highlight, you know, some of the features of what they do and the disguise coverages and things. Dave, I know this is kind of like an overarching question, but when you think about the totality of your program over the last three years, where do you view Chuba Hubard within that ecosystem uh that you've created here? >> Uh what I love about Chuba is that the things that we talk about wanting to be as an organization, he represents those in spades. Um his preparation, the way that he works, um the way I have to kind of reel him in and call him back a little bit because he goes so hard. He cares about every single part of of what it takes to play well on game day. And then he's a competitor on game day and he wants to win the down whatever is needed, the yards that are needed um in different games where we really need the run game to get going and Chuba showed up really big for us. And so um it's that mentality. It's why he's one of our captains, one of our leaders. Um because when he speaks it, he's just speaking it from a genuine place of what he cares about. Um, and I love I love when he gets up in front of the guys and uh and is able to to you know bring them together. >> Dave, do you anticipate then going into the game with with just two running backs or maybe will you bring one of those guys up from the practice squad or maybe whoever you sign if you >> Yeah, we'll we'll go in with three. It'll be Trey Trey Ty will be up this week. >> What kind of opportunity does this now present for a guy like AJ Dylan? >> A great opportunity. Um, while we still have Chuba being able to to handle the bulk of the carries, we are going to use that second back in different roles and AJ has done a great job for us and so this is a great opportunity for him. >> Dave, when you started calling plays, you were down on the sideline. Was there ever a temptation or did you ever consider calling from the booth or was that always where you wanted to be? >> I'm very comfortable on the sideline. Uh, some some guys prefer to be up in the box. It's it's uh pristine. It's it's very sterile up there sometimes and you can spread out all your sheets and kind of look at everything while you're calling it. Um I thought that was always interesting. I spent time in the box um as a QC just tracking charting plays, tracking coverages and those things like that. But um I always just enjoyed being on the sideline standing about 15 to 20 yards back behind the defense so I could get a feel for safety rotation. I could get a feel for are they chasing are they playing up the field that defensive end spot? You know, how deep are the linebackers? Are they up at the line of scrimmage right now on our runs? Does our play pass so I can get a feel for that right from the sideline? Um, and that's what I preferred. >> We'll do a couple more. The league's made like a conscious effort on offense to really get get bigger and most of it is with like loading up with tight ends around the line of scrimmage, but you guys have such big receiving options for Bryce and really on film against Atlanta really showed just how big these guys catch radiuses are and how they're able to play in their frames. How much does that help Bryce with just not having to be like necessarily perfect on every throw and having guys that he can trust to if he puts it maybe a little bit outside of their frame, they're able to go out there and get it. >> It is it's very helpful. Um I'll be honest, it it's not necessarily a philosophical belief of Dan and I. Um, we just want great players and as these players have come to us in the places where we drafted them or the guys that we signed, we were just looking for guys that were rugged, guys that fit our style of play, um, that really attack the ball. And they all happen to be monsters. And, you know, Xavier is the the little scat, you know, smaller slot type, you know, in our group, and he's 6'2, 225 pounds. And so then you throw Waller in there. Um, it's very friendly for the quarterback. And at the end of the day, like make the play however you need to make it and and understand big guys aren't going to run routes like the smaller fleet of foot guys. So, um, we have to understand that too and and fit the concepts for those guys and the routes that they do. Well, >> I don't think we have question. >> Phillips, can you give us some insight into >> his back flared up? Um, yeah, we're going to we're going to get him turn try to get him turned around pretty quickly, but um, he wasn't able to go today at practice, so um, he's getting worked on. He moved around uh before practice. they had him down there uh doing some dynamic movement and stuff. We thought it would be best to keep him out of the team periods and all those things. So, uh we'll keep working on him and and we'll give you updates as it goes. >> All right. Thank you. Oh, hey. Jack 3. Thank you. control. Everybody. Happy honey. afternoon. Yeah, it is the afternoon. Good point. Um, >> so Bryce, um, obviously Chuba predates you on the team, but when you think about this program, like it's the totality of the program that you guys have built with Dave and everybody else. Where do you think Chuba fits into that puzzle of creating the culture and and kind of getting the most out of you guys? >> Yeah, he's a huge uh tempo setter for us in everything that we do. Um, the way he carries himself, the way he works. Um, you can ask anyone in the locker room. uh you know, we all respect him by the way he goes about his business. Um out on the field, he's vocal. Um he's a he's a leader for us. Um you know, he's always bringing energy, always challenging us, pushing us to to be more. Um so, I mean, he's a huge part of who we are. Everything he he does, you know, exemplifies, you know, where where we're trying to go. So, yeah, I mean, he's he he's huge for us. >> You talked a lot in the preseason about how much it meant to see Jonathan coming back just as a human being. How hard is it to see him going IR with this now? >> Yeah. Um yeah. Uh I'm I feel for him. Um I'mma definitely be praying for him. Um again, he works so hard. Um yeah, it's it's tough. Um he he's a soldier. I know he's going to bounce back, do the work, um do everything. Um but uh yeah, like you said, from the human side, I just I feel for him. Um, yeah. >> How do you balance that? Like when you lose a guy to a major injury after a success on the field like that, like how do you you personally how do you deal with that? >> Um, I mean, you have to compartmentalize obviously, you know, you I have a lot of things that have to worry about. So, you you consume yourself with that. Obviously, be on the field, you have to go lead throughout the week, you have to go and do your job. Um, but yeah, I mean, of course, there's there's always that side that's um that's on your mind. Um, and it's it's just such a such a rough sport that we play. Um, you know, JB, everyone everyone across the league, I mean, it's just, you know, it's part of the game, unfortunately. Um, so yeah, I mean, my thoughts and prayers are with him, with anyone who's who's who's going through anything. Um, it's just, yeah, it's the unfortunate part of the game. >> Bryce, um, on a happier note, can you talk about why you think the offense is performing so well so far in the first two games? Um, yeah, I think it's just just uh trusting each other. Um, execution. Um, you know, Brad's doing a great job uh on game days and throughout the week of having a plan. Um, putting things together. Um, uh, all of us, you know, really buying into that, doing our 111th. Um, you know, being focused throughout the week. Um, you know, and that was the last two games. You know, we're 0 and0 this week. Uh, looking to be 1 and0. Um, we have to have a great week of practice. Um, you know, today was a good start, but we have to put them together. Again, it doesn't entitle you to anything when we get to Cleveland. It'll be zero to zero when we start. Um we we have to flush it. Um again, it's all about this week. So, we have a ton of respect for for them, a ton of respect for their their group as a defense. Uh we have to be at our best. So, right now, it's just um you know, all that stuff in the past in the past. Uh we have to earn the right to to go out and and try to have success this weekend. >> You're among the league leaders in a bunch of categories. Does that sort of thing matter to you? >> Uh no. Um we want to go one and0 this week. Um, again, stuff like that is I I I've always been, you know, I always care about what the people in this building think. I care about what's going on in this building. Um, you know, that's not going to change regardless of the circumstance. Uh, again, right now, all it all that matters is we want to go one and0 against Cleveland. Um, and we have a lot of work to do throughout the week to do that. Uh, myself, us as a team. Um, so that that's really where where my focus is at. >> Bryce, does this say anything to you about um this team losing big? title: HC Kevin Stefanski Post-game Press Conference | Week 3 | Falcons vs Packers
text: You know, had to be resilient on a short week. I thought we were and then very, very proud of the complimentary ball that was out there. Uh it starts with our special teams. I thought we covered kicks really well. And then just feeding off of each other. Our defense gets a huge stop there in the in the second half in the third quarter and uh our offense goes 90 to to uh really didn't put the game away by any stretch of imagination, but uh just showed that we're you know, that's something that we can do. Take the ball, uh whether it's by turnover and downs or otherwise and and go score touchdowns. So, proud overall the effort. Um it counts as one and we got to get back at it next week. With that, I'll take any questions. Yeah, you know, Mike's playing his first game, so you know there's going to be jitters. There's going to be you know, whether you call it rust, whatever it is and uh I don't think he expected to play perfect. I didn't expect him to play perfect, but I expected him to battle just like our football team and that's what he did. So, uh had some really nice moments in there. I thought protection by and large was really good and uh I thought Tommy did a great job of of giving him some um concepts that he's really comfortable with and then you know, Mike made great decisions with the ball. >> You called a bunch of screens there early in the second quarter. Was that maybe to get him in a rhythm with the play actions and >> I I think just in general Tommy did a nice job of spreading the ball around. I don't know how many guys touched the ball, but it seemed like a lot. Um and there are some defenses that will allow you to do that type of those type of plays, but some won't, so I really think it's just a matter of taking what was there. >> As a human being, how did you feel before Mike went in for Tommy? >> Yeah, I feel great for him and and I've told him this person, I've told you guys I'm proud of him. Uh it's not easy to rehab from injuries. This is that's that's a tough thing to do. Um what he's put himself through, the extra workouts in the weight room, the extra treatments in the training room, all those times that he's out in the field was running when no one was watching. You know, it's just him and and and the trainers. I give the medical staff a ton of credit. So, uh proud of all of that. I got to witness it. Um and it's and this tonight, you know, something you can build on. >> How do you think Michael did with as the outside noise kind of increased about 10 lbs and then kind of sticking his tongue out? >> Yeah, I regret to inform you we don't really listen to the outside noise. Uh you know, I know it's something I've been a fan. I get it, but we're really not concerned so much on outside noise. >> Can you discuss the play of the running backs with Jon Robinson and Brian Robinson today? >> Yeah, I thought their rush attack overall was outstanding. Uh really well designed by Tommy and Coach Callahan and uh any of those runs for what for them to work, it's it's got to be receivers blocking, tight ends blocking, and obviously the offensive line. So, uh I thought the guys were all on the same page. You know, we got a good run attack when we're headed up and we have a hat on a hat. Um and then give our runners the the free guys and I I thought that happened a bunch of times today and I thought Bijan and Brian were both outstanding. >> Good Zach blocked that kick. What did you guys have a small change there? What happened? >> Uh we didn't block a kick last year. And and that was uh that's something that we pride ourselves on as our field goal block unit. So, Zach's like 6'10 it seems. You got Gervon Dexter, um you got Mason. So, we got a bunch of guys. So, that should be a strength of ours. Um and when you block kicks, it's a pretty good correlation to winning. >> Did you have any shake-your-head moments tonight with Bijan? >> Probably. Yeah, I mean, it's fun to watch. Uh he's got a very unique style into how he runs the ball and and some of the stop and start and uh he does have the ability just to put his head down and and gain hard hard yards as well. Um yeah, he's he's somebody we're counting on. He's a team leader. Uh but what he does on the football field is pretty special. >> Nine for 194 from running, I I believe. >> Should have been more. >> Yeah. How much did you enjoy watching him though? He really You know, I told you guys and and Drake's a huge part of who we are and and when we're going to be at our best and and that's going to be, you know, tough each week to be at your best, but you have to be balanced and you have to be spreading the ball around. So, I thought he was where he was supposed to be a bunch of times. Mike made the the correct read and and made a bunch of plays. >> Do you think a win like this puts a statement out there that you were not who you >> I Yeah, I'm not big on on those type of things. I I I think every week in the NFL is hard. It's just hard. And next the next week's going to be hard and the next one after that. So, we don't ride the roller coaster in our building. We just stay focused on what's in front of us. >> To that point, you said last week the week before I believe about that's not the standard of of what we're playing. >> Sure. >> Why is this more like it? >> Well, I I would start with playing complimentary ball. Uh you know, what did the turnover margin end tonight? I know we gave it away once. We got one. Is that right? So, we're even. Now, we had the return over on downs there. I know they don't officially count, but when you're even, at least you have a chance. And when you lose, it makes it really hard. Lose the margin, it makes it hard. So, I think the message for our football team will continue to be to do all those things that allow you to win the turnover margin and allow you to play complimentary ball. >> So, how about we take a couple more with two on that final touchdown yesterday? Just just the math of that. >> Yeah, it's the math. Just get to 21. Um you know, I look across the field, I see Jordan Love and that pass attack. I just want to make sure that we're at 21. >> You had Jordan Love I think 12 times and allowed under 20 rushing yards. How how happy are you? >> Yeah, outstanding. Like I told them, they harassed the quarterback and you know, I don't know what the the sacks say and I think sacks can be liars. Um listen, we love to get sacks whenever we can, but you want to pressure the quarterback and I thought he was under pressure quite a bit. >> You mentioned not riding the roller coaster, but I mean games like this on the road serve as a springboard. >> You know, we're trying to just go one and oh each week, Jeremy, and I'm very proud of the effort. Uh I'm very proud of the effort on a short week, and uh a lot of what the results you see on a night like this really happen on Monday, and they happen on Tuesday. So, uh I know what this football team is made of. I know uh how they approach their job, uh and we'll just focus and keep our head down and and worry about what's in front of us. >> Thanks, coach. >> Thank you, guys.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | September 25th, 2026
text: Just talk about you know what Nick Chubb meant to this football team and and how great it was for you to be able to have the chance to coach him. >> Yes, I I was only around Nick for a year. Obviously after year when I went back to Georgia, you hear the stories of you know Nick Chubb. I mean when you think about his first 2 years at Georgia averaging like 7 and 8 yards a carry. And doesn't It was interesting we just had him speak to the team which is interesting cuz he really doesn't say much. He really just he speaks with his work and his play. And um you know, the the weekly prep uh will take care of will take care of the Sundays. >> Hayson and Grant, just how do you envision the next 48 hours for for those two guys as question them all right now? >> Yeah, we'll see. Uh they went through practice today and and we'll see we'll see where they're at. I think you mentioned Monday that you thought he played better week two than he did week one. I mean, there was so many things that that we could do better. And you know, I think Mason understood that and we all understood that and and I expected him to play better. There wasn't any one thing in particular. Uh we just did things better. You know, schematically we did things uh you know, operationally on both sides and uh so and and we certainly did a better job of winning our one-on-ones. Mason was was was also part of that. >> Next man up league, but Devin Lloyd not being on that Panthers defense, being being ruled out, just how much does that alter what they do defensively? >> Well, first of all, um he's a tremendous player. I got a lot of respect for him. But I have a lot of respect for their staff and that that that's the NFL, you know. Uh you have to have next man up and be ready to play and and um I did not know that. So, you're telling me that now, so I did not know that and but we we prepared for the Carolina Panthers and he's a part of that. And we'll continue to pre- prepare over the next 40 hours 48 hours, put our best foot forward. >> Now, obviously with the young team, you got to prepare after you get blown out week one, how are they going to respond to that loss? In the same breath, with the young team, assuming you got to prepare them for, you know, not reading their press clippings after a strong week two win. So, what kind of goes into that? What's the message from you this week to make sure the guys um aren't too loud? >> Well, it's it's it's a week-to-week league. We all know that, you know, and we're playing against the best in the world every single weekend. We're coaching it's against the best in the world. We're playing against the best in the world. And the bottom line is as I told the team and I told you guys that, okay, so what now what, right? Can you [clears throat] really refocus in terms of the development piece, all of us, um strategically coaching and then playing. That's our job is to create the best version of our players, develop them, and in turn the further they develop, the fur- further we'll develop as a team. And we've had a great week of practice. Well, we always have. And what we do is we'll take care of our bodies today, get rest, fuel and hydrate, we'll come back and walk tomorrow. And uh we'll be ready to go on Sunday. And and we'll see. I mean, that's what it is. I mean, we we go out there and I love the way we fight and I love the way we compete, and uh I look forward to the challenge cuz that's really good football team. And I think we are, too. We'll give our We'll put our best foot forward again. >> What have you seen from Deshaun Watson in his preparation this week? How has he looked in practice this week? >> Uh I mean, he's had his best week. You know, he really has. And I think that that's been building. I think that's been building from becoming the starter after the first week, being disappointed um the second half that he played last week. And I think I mean, you'd have to speak to him, but I think his confidence, and it should be at an all-time high, you know, in the excitement of of an opportunity, a third opportunity, um to continue to to just grow and develop as a player cuz again he's he's just scratching the surface the last couple day the couple weeks. >> Kind of in '19 when the season ended Nick Chubb went to the 4:00 games leading the league in rushing and he got beat by Derrick Henry. How cool is it that you got to coach both of those guys? >> Boy, that's a lot of fun. You know, I mean it's uh I've I've been blessed to be around a lot of great football players and great coaches. And that that's fun to be around because you grow, you know, you grow and those guys are are different. You know, Derrick and and Nick are different. And cuz Derrick doesn't say much. He just speaks by his work and his play. And that's where the respect comes from is you don't have to say a lot like anything in life. It's really what we do not what we say. Right? It's it's our actions that speak louder than words. We've been told that since we were little. Right? Everybody told us that and those guys are the epitome of that. >> Coach, when you talk about the week-to-week thing, do you think it takes some guys some young guys a while to kind of understand that the NFL is that you know, week-to-week we see the last night's game, right? You pointed to watching the example of my cousin. Do you think it takes guys to appreciate a little bit to appreciate that? >> Um I think every player's got to whether they're young or old have to deal with the scrutiny that we're under and the player's ability to compartmentalize what's out there. And uh stay humble or you're going to get humbled. And that's just the way it is. I mean, stay humbled. Keep fighting for what you want. Don't worry about the record, it'll take care of itself. title: Zac Taylor Press Conference - September 23
text: [music] >> All right, first I'll start with injuries. Andre Yoshi lost two ligaments thumb had surgery this morning. He'll be on IR. It'll be a week's issue. It's not a season-long issue, but it'll definitely be the IR window. Plus maybe a little bit more, but don't have a time on on that yet. So, unfortunately for him. And then other otherwise BJ Hill will continue to work him through the week and see where he ends up for this game. As we manage him, Jonathan Allen will be out today load load management. And um I think that was it. If there's any other questions on guys, you can let me know. >> When did that occur just in the game? >> Some point in the game, yeah. >> Are you all going to call how are you all going to handle it? >> We'll see. I have nothing I'll say today, but um we'll be able to manage through that. >> Will Joe practice today? >> He's sore, so we'll we'll see how he gets through practice today. But we'll see when he gets out there. >> Is the soreness related to the back? >> I don't know. I don't I think it's just overall sore from the game. >> How was that what's that competition like earlier in the week in terms of how what what what is load management going to be like on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday? When are you all going to have that conversation on what you can and can't do? >> For the D lineman? >> No, for Burrow. >> Oh, we'll just see how he feels. >> Is the opportunity with Yoshi being down that presents it for the other guys who can step in here? >> Yeah, several guys that can step up. Um whether it's in the receiver room, tight end room. There's a lot of ways we're going to fill that, but um we have guys that will step up. They're going to get be given more opportunity and and expect those guys to step up and fill those shoes. >> Any look at Pittsburgh's defense what kind of jumps out at you guys playing so long? >> Yeah, great tremendous front. They've really invested a lot in the front. Those guys are playing at a really high level, all of them. Uh Sometimes you're waiting on these guys to to descend in their career, and they've never done that. You know, they just keep seeming like they're getting better, so that's where you guys start. They got a lot of talent behind them, you know, at the linebacker and DB position as well. So, nobody you take for granted. Got a lot of respect for Patrick Graham. I think he does a great job as a coordinator, so makes the defense really challenging. Played them a couple years ago when he was in the Raiders, so really good unit. Obviously a lot of talent on offense as well. So, work cut out for us on defense, and then specialist, you know, their kicker made a I think 57-yarder last week, and he's always been great, so really challenges in all three phases that our guys got to be ready for. >> How is the defense How is the defense How is [snorts] the defense different this first time under, you know, they haven't been under Tomlin for almost 40 years? >> Yeah, I mean, I think overall it's it's a different scheme. It's Patrick Graham's scheme. There are some of the same trademarks that have always shown up with the with the Steelers' defense, and particularly up front. so, there's there's things you have to manage, you know, with the tape that's available to you from their time this year and time from past years. Um so, we're doing our best to work through that. Have a great plan. >> Is it going to be weird looking across the sideline and not seeing Mike Tomlin? >> It is It's still strange, you know, I think. This is the first time I'll have to deal with that. Um he had such a tremendous run there, and he's doing a great job on TV. He's entertaining to watch, too, you know, and so um it is a little bit different without him being over there, but Coach Gase and Mike McCarthy in the past, too, so that won't be anything new. >> You talked to Graham pretty seriously when the DC job was open. >> Yeah, Patrick Graham. >> What What What did you What impressed you about him? >> Well, I didn't know him as a person, you know, obviously you interview him because you're impressed with the scheme, and and the problems he you face when you're against them. Um I think when you meet him, um incredibly personable, a lot [snorts] of confidence, a lot of respect for the game, a lot of respect for the offenses, you know, and and kind of the the waves of offenses that are coming through and some of the tendencies people develop and and scheme patterns that show up. And so, really enjoyed my time with him. Thought highly of him. Thought highly of him before. Thought even probably highly of him even more so afterwards and um he's in our division now, so that's what we got in front of us. >> Does he have a lot of uh does he have similar traits with Flores? What Flores does? I mean, they >> Um I don't know that they've ever crossed over. No, I wouldn't say that. >> T.J. Watt is going to be 32 in a couple weeks. >> they did they were in Miami together. Yeah, they're some tend Sorry, you got me off really threw me off with that one right there. Um Yeah, they're I mean, they they're I even played I guess we played Flores last year. I'm just going to skip that question cuz I get totally got thrown off there. >> Sorry about that. On on film, does T.J. Watt look like he's tweaked the way he goes about things or does things or is he still look like 25-year-old T.J. >> He still looks like he's right in his prime. So, again, he's I think what he's got four sacks this year, four or five sacks this year. A lot of pressures, a lot of hits. Affects the quarterback, affects the run game. So, I mean, that that's the part I think where tip balls, you know, I'm and there's obviously stat one, but how much they affect that part of the game. So, it's not just the sacks, not just the hits, it's the tip balls, you have the interception for the touchdown against Atlanta. and we've seen him do that before to us as well. So, and then just the run game is really challenging over there as well, whether he's on the front side or the back side. Just the physicality he plays with and the pursuit on the back side. So, he he shows up in every area of the game. And so, you certainly got to be aware of him, but he's not the only one. They got they got a lot of guys that are really good. And um So, again, our guys are got to be up for the challenge and it'll be a fun opportunity for them. >> Seemed like those tip balls were more [snorts] prevalent in earlier in Joe's career, not just for T.J., but across the board. Is that something he just worked himself out of? Is Is the O-line improving or what what on there? >> It's given I it's sometimes it can be a play-by-play situation. It's what play you have. Um sometimes some D-linemen can kind of read into how they're being set by the linemen, and they drop the quarterback, and and so I I hate to say it's something drastically has changed for quarterback because every game's a little bit unique. Um these guys are just really good at understanding maybe when they're not going to win in the rush, or something tells them the ball's coming out, and they get their hands up. Heyward's excellent. I mean, Heyward had like 40 four tips in the first 46 plays this season. I mean, he was getting his hands all over the ball, and several other guys have as well. So, something that they're really good at, and and we got to do a good job of combating that. >> Something seems like the Steelers have a lot of size in their receivers. Obviously, they have DK. Pat Freiermuth has always done really well against you guys. Darnell Washington had a big game in Pittsburgh last year. What makes them so good? >> Their receivers and tight ends, they're very talented, you know, and Pittman as well. We don't know what his status is, but he's a big receiver as well. So, um they've got a lot of talent. They're doing a good job that way. Their tight ends can, you know, um Freiermuth does a good job getting down the field, making big plays. Darnell catches the ball underneath, and makes you pay for it underneath as well. So, he's hard to bring down. He's really good in the run game as well. He's got good hands. Um and then obviously DK's one of the top receivers in the league, very physical. Um so, he's he's just so powerful with how he moves, and uh as you have to defend him. And, you know, Pittman's obviously had a tremendous career as well, and we'll see what his status is, but um he's got really good hands, good awareness, really smart receiver. And then they got, you know, one of the all-time greats at quarterback. So, it's very challenging. >> Going back to Burrow for a second, do you have to see how he looks today to see what tomorrow's going to look like, or do you already know what tomorrow will be like for him? >> I I don't know what tomorrow we'll see today how it goes. >> What's the staple [snorts] of the Mike McCarthy-Aaron Rodgers offense? >> What is the staple of the Mike McCarthy-Aaron Rodgers offense? Um we'll see. I mean, they're two games in right now, so I'm not going to make any predictions about what they're going to be for the rest of the season. Um, you know, I know that that they're very much in sync and like any offensive guy that calls the plays with the quarterback, there's a lot of communication there. Um, so you got to see the offense through the same lens. They've obviously had a lot of history there uh, to be able to do that. So, uh, he he gets a lot of freedom at the line, which I think Aaron's kind of always had from coach to coach, but um, I think that's important, you know, for for veteran quarterbacks that have a good command of what they're seeing and what their offense is to give them that freedom to do things like that. And Joe's got that freedom with us. I've always seen Aaron have that freedom with them. So, it is it's tough challenge. They know each other well, so it's not like a new scheme for him. It's a new scheme in the sense that, you know, they're doing it here with the Steelers and new players and they're all coming together there, but um, I would imagine that, you know, it's it's it's going to be very difficult to deal with over the course of the season. >> Seems to me inside the locker room, Zach, there's this feeling of no satisfaction from a good training camp, from a good preseason, from a two and 0 start. How important is it to have that kind of mindset just continuing week to week in a locker room? >> You You Can you say at the beginning of the >> That no satisfaction >> No satisfaction. Okay, got it. Yeah, well, that's you know, we haven't played any of the season yet. You know, we're we're two games down, 15 left. Um, so if you start thinking we we've arrived, we've played no divisional games, no road divisional games, really nothing. We we've given ourselves a little bit of a head start coming out of training camp with these first two games, but that's it. And so, I think for our guys to understand, you know, you you get a chance to prove yourself when you go on a road divisional game. That that's your first real opportunity to see what you're about. We've been trailing for what 4 minutes of the season so far, so we really haven't faced adversity in that way where, you know, something something went sideways on us and now we got to dig ourselves out of a hole. We haven't had to do that yet. So, I think I know what I'll see from our team, but um, tho- those bits of adversity haven't come yet. And I know going in this environment it's going to be very challenging. We got to get our players ready for that. Um we got to do a much better job with the penalties, especially on offense, not setting ourselves back. You know, if you really look into the two games they played, that's happened a little bit um in the first game of the season with them, so um we got to do a great job, take care of the things that we can control pre-snap. >> Exactly. >> Thank you. >> Thanks. >> [snorts]

title: Postgame Press Conferences
text: Heat. Heat. Heat. Hey, Heat. Natalie Hey. Hey. Hey. Hey. Hey. Hey, Everybody get me. Well, that was a humbling night. Um, certainly I don't think anybody's pleased about this. Um, and you know, we we've got a couple extra days here and everybody's got to take a long hard look at themselves and we got to find solutions and just come back ready to work. Um, but it it certainly was a tough night. >> How do you fix the offensive line? >> Again, I just I think we got to continue to work with these guys and and try to figure out what we do well because right now I don't know what we're doing well offensively. So, um, you know, I think we can all see the benefit of of having a strong rushing attack, uh, how you can get into normal rhythm on offense and that will open up a lot of things in the passing game. But anytime you drop back 50 some odd times in a game and you have nine rushes, it's it's usually not going to bode well for you. >> Matt, I'm not in the meetings, but just given on how the Lions played through three games, at what point do you have to consider making a change with the coaching staff there? Oh, I'm I'm I'm I'm not going to respond to that question. How >> much does not Josh hurt the running game? >> I mean, I think we all saw a dynamic running back on the other side and I think Josh is a dynamic running back, but it it is the situation. It's it's the circumstance and um it is what it is right now and we got to find a way to just try to either well one we got to put them in a better position and then those guys got to go do it. Do you need some uh help from the outside, you think, for Brian to go get some? >> I'm not I'm not going to get any of that stuff right now without taking a peek at the tape and and doing all that. Um I just I'm I'm going to work with who's ever here and we're going to all work together to try to fix this thing. I mean, it's three games in certainly we're nowhere near where we need to be and uh but there's a lot of ball left in front of us. you know, maybe just because there is the running game for Penn, but he had a lot of easy completions, it seemed like. It seems like Jordan just doesn't have those. Is that a fair assessment? How do you get Jordan to get some of those easy ones? >> Yeah, I think you know, you're absolutely right. We took some shots early on, try to loosen them up. They were squatting on a lot of our routes, especially on the outside, and we didn't connect. So, um, that that's what it was. >> You guys started off really strong, both sides of the ball, and then after that roughing it seemed to really turn. What do you think about just the resiliency or I guess lack thereof of of the adversity in that moment? >> Well, I mean, I don't want to say that that was the reason that we lost. I mean, any I mean, they had 500 yards of offense. We had whatever it was. Um, it was it was a boat whooping. So, I'm not going to put it on one thing. Uh certainly we definitely have to respond better, but that was at least three quarter butt whooping right there. >> Matt, you mentioned, you know, not knowing what you do well on offense right now. As a play caller, do you have some core concepts you feel like you can maybe lean on from the past or anything like that? >> Yeah, sure. We we feel like we have a lot of concepts that we can lean on. Um, but you know, give give a lot of credit to Atlanta and and some of these other defenses we played. Uh, we just were not always executing and certainly there's some times where we got some bad play calls. I mean, it's it's all of us. >> Defense have been pretty solid first two games. What do you think happened there? >> Yeah, I mean, I got to go back and watch the tape. I don't want to say anything out of turn. Um, but certainly I do think that that was a pretty dynamic running back. Um, if I would if what do you have 194 yards rushing? Um, anytime you do that, it's going to be tough to win games in this league. So, >> what did you think of roughing the passer call that allowed the Falcons to get back on the field and score their first? >> I'm not going to answer that. I'm I'm not going to get fined. >> Matt, you talked to Jagger when he came off the field after the false start on the fourth down. Were you planning on snapping that ball or were you just trying to get him to jump? >> Yeah, there was it was no snap, no play. And that it's just, you know, a young player that hasn't been in there. So, I think it's a good learning lesson. I think we'll all learn from that and um you know, I don't think I don't anticipate it happening again. So, in all the years you've coached, have you have you been in a situation where you just don't feel like you have an understanding of what your offensive line is capable of giving you to allow you to function as an offense? Does it feel like that right now? And >> no, I I don't want to put all the blame on the offensive line. I mean, there's plenty of blame to go around. We got to catch the ball better. Um, certainly there's some throws I I think Jay Love would love to have back, and I just like there's some play calls I I would love to have back. uh most notably that you know we're still in the game um and we drive down to start the second half we have a fourth and one and it's gloved. So um it's just there's enough blame to go around to everybody. >> What was the message to the locker room tonight >> to you got three days to decompress and and we got to get back to work and I fully anticipate I I don't just knowing the guys in that locker room uh we know it's going to get loud. you got to ignore the noise um and just focus on what we can do better. I think we all collectively have individually uh have something that we can get better at and so it's just roll up your sleeves and get to work. >> You guys have gone through stretches like this before in your time here. What what about this group makes you think that they can get out the other side of Yeah, I just think we got the right kind of guys that that aren't afraid of the work, that aren't afraid of the challenge, that aren't afraid to to attack adversity and um I fully anticipate our guys doing that. >> You you always talk about how even Keel Jordan is and that's a good thing. Is there a value in him maybe and I don't want to not be himself, but is there a value in him maybe getting after guys a little bit or maybe being a little more demonstrative? >> Yeah, I I don't want to like you don't want people to be somebody they're not. So, um because then I think it's disingenuous and I think he's he's a great leader. I think that he's got definitely got the respect of everybody in that locker room and it's not like he might not he definitely is not afraid to you know say something to somebody but he does it in his own way which I appreciate and I think the guys do do as well. >> The last drive on offense with Jordan still out there with the score the way it was. Is that just to get as many reps with this O line and this group trying to find something or >> Yeah, we're just trying to get something going like try to play I mean you're just trying to play play your way out of it and certainly I knew the risk there. Um I never liked seeing him get hit like that. Um and yeah, so we that's why we we kept rolling. >> Do you worry at all about Jordan's clock getting sped up with what he's kind of encountered through these first three weeks? Yeah, I mean I absolutely I think that's tough on a quarterback if if you're constantly getting hit and throwing off your back foot and um you know it's hard to trust everything that's going on around you. Um but we also got to look at things that we can do schematically to help alleviate some of that pressure. Like I said, if if you would have told me we're going to drop back 50 some odd times, I would say it's probably not a good night for us. Um, I think you need to have some semblance of a a running game to complement the pass game, at least to keep people on their heels so they just don't tee off and get at after the quarterback. >> I was just on that really quickly here. We're now three games into the season and you've had Johnson, Lloyd, and Brooks uh carry the ball in various instances throughout the game. Do you have a legitimate one running back one at this point three weeks in? >> Yeah, I'm I'm not going to answer that right now. I think everybody's in competition. the fourth and one tonight. Obviously, two weeks ago, Minnesota went with QB sneak there. Was the pass in that situation directly tied to not getting it? >> No, not at all. Actually, it was a it was a canned play and you know, if you get the look, you you run the pass. They did a good job defending it. It's something we saw on tape. Obviously, didn't work. >> All of your plays to look like, you know, kind of the same that illusion of complexity when you're unable to run it. How much does that affect your ability to get into some of your play action? >> A lot. >> How much of your offense do you feel like you can utilize and access right now? >> I don't even understand that question. >> Are there plays that given how the protection is given given the issues that you guys are having that you just feel like are off the table that ordinarily would be? >> Not not necessarily. I think it's a combination of when you dial them up and how you got go out there and execute them. Thank you guys. >> Thanks guys. Have a good night. >> Thank you. hey, hey. Hey. You guys started strong tonight. Both sides of the ball were playing well. What What changed? Because it wasn't like this from the beginning. Um man, I think uh offensively, you know, had the touchdown drive like you said, um and just really couldn't get into a groove after that. Just a lot of just couldn't execute um and couldn't make plays out there. So, um a lot of stuff that wasn't good and you know, we couldn't get into a groove I feel like and uh you know, it was a couple maybe a good play here and then a couple bad plays after that. So, something that we got to look at, dive into what we're doing good, dive into what we're not doing good. Um, and obviously there's a lot of stuff that we need to improve on. Um, myself to start with for sure. So, >> what are you doing well? >> Something we'll look at, see what plays were were running well. Um, >> go from that. Is there anything you guys can hang your head on, you think? Or >> Yeah, I think there's uh there's definitely a couple plays that uh are we're doing well and I think there's a lot of plays that the execution is not where it needs to be. Um from a lot of positions and it's just something that we got to keep looking at and keep improving on. Um but I can't pinpoint that there's one thing I would say right now that we're doing well. Um I think there's a lot of things we just need to improve on. Jordan Matt said the next three days are for the players to decompress and then get back ready to work. Are you going to be able to decompress for three days or do you try to let it go? Do you look at the film a million times on your own? How do you handle this? >> Yeah, I definitely think it's uh it's a very disappointing feeling right now. Um you know, how we went out and played today. Um like I said, myself to start um a lot of stuff to improve on, to get better at and to look at. So I think yeah, we'll we'll take the three days. I think we'll all be reviewing the film and I think everybody's got to look theirelves in the mirror and see where we can improve as individuals and as a as a unit, as a offense, what we can improve on. Um, but you know, I think take three days, get your body back. But I think mentally, uh, a lot of stuff we'll need to look at. >> You said twice now for yourself to start when it comes to playing better. What things specifically are you self-critical of? Because from the outside looking at it, it looks like a situation that would be tough. quarterback given the protection issues, drop passes, all those things. So, what things are you thinking about need to be better from your end? >> Man, a lot of stuff. Um, you know, I think to start my footwork in the pocket, I think, uh, making accurate throws. Um, my decision- making and reads, going through those things quickly. Um, so I think, you know, just the feeling I have right now is not good. Um, I think a a lot of areas we need to improve, but at the end of the day, I just sit here and look at myself and say there's so much stuff I can improve on to make us as a offense better. Um, it always starts with me, you know, to be the leader of the team. I've got to improve and be better in a lot of areas. There's a lot of stuff that I'll look at on film that, um, I won't be happy with, you know, how I performed tonight. So, um, like I said, you know, it's kind of the feeling, especially last week, too. A lot of stuff to keep improving on. And like I mentioned, it's just it's about getting back to the drawing board as a unit, figuring out where everybody can improve. Um, but for me, all I can do is look myself in the mirror and see where I can get better for the team. >> I was just saying that considering the barrage of pressure that you've been under, he's worried about the clock obviously not speeding up too much. How difficult is that to keep the same timing you'd have otherwise when you don't have the protection that you would have otherwise? >> Yeah, you know, I think uh it is difficult. Um, you know, I think that's where I can improve at making quicker decisions, understanding the coverages, and where I can get the ball out and find completions. You know, I got to do a better job of just finding completions throughout the course of the game to help us stay on track as a offense and stay out of some of these, you know, bad situations, third and long, second and long. So, um, you know, I think there's always, it's NFL, like since I've been here, there's always going to be plays where there's going to be pressure. Sometimes you might have a little more time in the pocket. Um, but as a quarterback, I got to operate a lot faster and be more accurate and just find completions to help us as offense. >> I'm not sure how much you watch the other quarterback play, but see like Penn said, a lot of easy completions, whether the receiver screens or slants. Seems like every time you go back to the pocket, there's just nothing easy there. Does it feel hard when you go back there or is just you always chering completions? Is it hard to find them? Yeah, I think I mean you look at this game tonight, I think, you know, we got behind. Um, and I think our run game's got to improve. I think when you have a a solid, you know, pass game and run game kind of balancing each other, um, that always helps, you know, it helps alleviate, makes the defense a little more on their toes. Um, and I feel like obviously our run game, I don't know how many rushes we had, but um, it's something that we need to improve on right there. I think that will help the pass game. Um, and then I think like you said, when we do have those easy completions, we got to hit those. You know, we're not we're not executing those at a high level right now. Um, some gimmies that we we left out there today. Um, but I think we just got to we got to be more complimentary as offense and tonight was was definitely not that. >> Since you've been here, you guys have been pretty balanced between Josh and Aaron Jones and all those guys. with you not able to do that so far this season. Do you have to fight the urge of trying to do too much because the only way that you're gaining yards is in, you know, drop back passing or in the passing >> Definitely. You always got to fight the urge to to do too much as a quarterback. I think you look at the the game tonight when you get down, that's really all you can do. You have to go out there, find ways to make plays and uh put up points in a hurry. We didn't do that. Um, so like I said, it starts early on in the game is executing better early on, putting up points, helping our defense out, being able to stay on the field, execute third downs, and um, like you said, get a little bit more balance with the run game in the pass game. But, um, you know, I think we got behind tonight and, uh, didn't just it didn't look good. >> You drive down there and have the the fourth and one attempt. what went into that play from your perspective? >> Yeah, I think they did a good job defensively. Um, guarding the play. Um, it's one of those ones I want to look back and see, you know, what I could have done better, what we could have done better as a unit right there. Um, you know, and look at it. But, you know, when I came out, I didn't feel like we had a lot of options that were open right there. I felt like I kind of had pressure. Um, you know, I might be we'll see when I look at it, but um see what else we could have done differently right there. Um, but yeah, >> second time this season that you had a hot start and the score got out of hand after that happened last season, too. Do you feel like there's a resiliency problem with this team? Does that need to be something that improves over this weekend to become more resilient as a group? Yeah, I mean I think it's just an execution problem right now more than anything. Um, you know, it's a close game and I feel like we went out there on offense and consistently couldn't put drives together, couldn't stay on the field and that's not a it's not a good recipe at all. So, um, it's not a great feeling uh, you know, as a offense to have repeated drives that don't go anywhere, but at the end of the day, we got to still fight. You know, we've been in games before where we've came back and it's all about continuing to fight. I think guys did that, but I think the execution is just it's not where it needs to be at all. And uh we we'll we'll dig deep to see. Um but, you know, when we're not making any big plays, um you know, we got to find something that's going to bring the energy and uh you know, we got to figure out what that's going to be. >> Is is it too much explosive player bust on offense right now? I mean, when you had your good moments tonight, it was explosive, right? >> Mhm. Yeah. I think that's that's what I'm talking about with execution. Um, you know, we we have a couple big plays and we're not just stacking stuff on top of each other. You know, usually you get a big play, it leads to points and it leads to big drives and we might have a big play that ends with no points. So, um, yeah, I think, uh, there's a lot of stuff that needs clean up, but I think just the consistency on offense is is not where it needs to be, and I think that'll help change a lot of things. Um, and just figuring out what we can do better, what we can do well, and keep leaning on those things. >> What gives you the confidence that Matt and the staff can find those answers over the next three days to get you guys going? >> Yeah, I think it's it's not just over the next three days. I think it's we have a long season ahead of us and it's a it's a long journey. We know that. Um but I I always have confidence in Matt. I've been with him for so long and I've seen what what we can do as offense. I've seen what the the highs look like as offense and uh that's the most frustrating part is um we're not there and we're not we're not playing at that level right now that I know we can play at. So, um, like I said, there's there's always going to be stuff as play callers you look back and say, "I wish we would have done this different." As a quarterback, I wish I would have done different. So, we'll we'll dive deep and and like I said, it's a it's a it's a long season of continuing to figure out where we can get better. Um, but I still got confidence in everybody in that locker room, man. >> Two more face. the challenge you face to prevent the frustration from turning into a greater negative as you roll forward. >> Um, man, I think, uh, it's one of those things you got to take day by day. Um, like I said, we're very frustrated tonight with the performance. Um, but I think the positive is knowing that there's still a lot of ball out there for us. And, uh, I think as a unit, we all got to stick together. Um, you know, I think we always look back to the 2023 season. Um, you know, my first year starting, it didn't start well that season as well. And we started figuring stuff out. Started getting rolling. Um, and we got hot. So, there's still a lot of ball out there in front of us. Um, no one's no one's, you know, throwing in the the towel at all. You know, it's just we got a lot of work to do to to get better as a team um and as offense. So, um, you know, it's just about continuing to find the positives and what we're doing. Um, so, yeah. >> Does this feel like 2023 just from the lack of answers that you have right now? >> Uh, man, every year feels different to be honest. Um, and this year just I I'll say right now looking at the game tonight, it's frustrating. Um, there's no nothing around it. I'm I'm frustrated. Um, like I said, I just I look back at what I can do better as a quarterback of this team, as a leader of this team. Um, but, uh, to start the season, it's not great. I'll say that. And, uh, it's only up from here. You know, we got to we got to keep improving. Like I said, we got a long season, so it's back to the drawing board. We always say we take it one day at a time, one week at a time, focus on the next opponent, and that's all we can do right now. Last one before >> Matthew Golden finally getting in the end zone for the, you know, first regular season career touchdown. How much do you think that will help him lift the weight off his shoulders and really blossom as a wide receiver? >> Um, I think it was great. I think he made a fantastic catch on that touchdown. I thought the other third down early in the game, the big play, fantastic catch. So, um, I think for him, there's a lot of stuff that he did well. And it's, like I said, for us as a unit. I'm sure there's stuff that he feels maybe he can improve on and and do better. Like I said, I think it's just everybody looking at each other and figuring out what we can do better as individuals, but I think MG made some some fantastic plays for sure. Um, but I think as a unit, we just got to get better. That's it. Sure. Thank you.

Um, so I think that we'll continue to work on our fundamentals. Uh, but it's something that I'm not going to overdo with the guys because then I think it becomes a negative. Um, you know, it looked like maybe at least each time. >> Yeah, I think whenever there's a drop, it's it's a variety of things. You know, it's it's focus on the football. You know that the energy whether it's in the meeting room, in the walkthrough or on the field, I believe that is so important to a football team to have energy, to have positive juice, as I say, and like we we just make it really easy with the receivers. So, um, definitely try to keep our quarterback um, keep him with us.
