So, >> it creates a disparity of competition >> because people want to go to where they get paid more. >> You know what I mean? And so it's like right now it's like who can pay the most and I'm all for players getting paid. It's just more so of like even the playing field because now it's more so about what teams has the most money and that's who is kind of you you see the trajectory of who is in the top 20 is mostly the teams who have the most money. >> Would you uh have wanted to deal with that when you were >> Absolutely. [laughter] I would have want to be a part of this. Like I probably wouldn't have stayed in college 6 years cuz coming [laughter] out of college 24 25 is a little h you know I always had goals of playing in the NFL for 15 to 20 years but I I definitely would have loved to be a part of this this NIL thing going on. You know what I mean? >> C you know you have to collectively bargain it. One of the things you guys get as a union with the players limits on how much you can practice the pads and all that. How nice would that be to be a part of the players down in college? >> I think it'll be huge. I mean, um I think you got to take that in consideration now as especially with these players making so much money. Um the best uh ability is availability. And the way college goes, you can have two a day still. I think I I'm not really for sure on that answer, but if that's if that's the case, then you got to kind of reconsider that, especially with how much players are getting paid. These guys are making more than rookies in the NFL these days. So, that would be uh something you have to consider, especially playing in the SEC or the Big 10, which is two of the most competitive leagues in college. He mentioned that you being a big part of that working with you previously. He, you know, hit his career his career long on Sunday in the stadium that he used to play in. What was that moment like for him? I think when players know that you're authentic and they know that you're pulling for them, but you're also going to correct them when something's wrong, and not just you know, there's a lot of coaches that um correct uh rookies loudly, but they don't say anything to vets. I think you got to be consistent and correct everybody the same way. So, hopefully that uh authenticity, that's a big word for me, uh comes through for them. >> All right, next question. >> Thank you. Appreciate y'all. >> Thanks, coach. Appreciate it.

text: Good morning. >> Uh, I'm going to just go through >> Who's out Sunday? >> Uh, is Caleb out Sunday? >> Caleb Douglas will be out on Sunday. >> Okay. You guys would probably like it a lot better. >> Did Brian Miller suffer the injury in practice or is that something that was lingering from the game? >> You know, it's been something that's just been lingering and we just wanted to give it some rest to let it kind of calm down. We have different players playing. I think for the most part, it will be very, very similar, but there'll be some tweaks in there with different guys having different roles and uh some guys now having a chance, you know, to step up and play. >> I know the communication issues last week were a bit frustrating. How have you seen the team take ownership of the of those issues this week? >> Yeah, I mean, communication issues for a young group of guys playing out there, it's not Is it frustrating? Sure, but is that um you know, uncommon? No. I mean, it's just it's a position of guys playing back there for the first time that they're going to have to constantly grow together. Um that's what practice is for. That's what walk-throughs are for. That's what meeting togethers are for. And I just I've seen those guys work really hard at it this week. You know, to try to to try to get it better, you know? >> What can you tell us about the status of Beal and Brass? >> Yeah, Beal will be out and Juju will practice today. >> What I wanted to ask you about the the twists and stunts from defensive linemen, front seven guys. Yesterday I was asking uh Shawn and he was talking about it's it's much like the secondary in terms of communication and chemistry. How do you develop that when you're pretty much a new crew that has to get there? >> I think it's like with anything else. We just need We need time and we need repetition. And then all of a sudden, you're right, when you bring a new guy in, you need more time and you need repetition. So, we have to try to We I I've said this before um and you've asked this quite a bit. I mean, we need to develop, right? So, we need to find extra time to work on all of these things. Um give you an example, yesterday. Yesterday we did we did a developmental seven-on-seven for guys who were not getting enough reps because we need to do that. So, when practice was done, there were certain guys who you know, didn't get a whole lot of reps running our scheme, maybe the opponent's team, so we kept them after and we played football together. Quarterback, wide receivers, DBs communicating. We're going to do the same thing with the guys on Sunday who are not active for the game. And we're going to take those guys and we're basically going to have a practice in the morning. We're going to do individual, we're going to do special teams, we're going to do a group period for exactly what you're just saying. We need to We need to develop cuz we're going to need these new guys entering different positions as we go. Um, so the big theme I keep saying is we need to develop, we need time, we need extra work, we have to think outside the box on how to get that work done. And and that's what we were working really hard on, whether it's communication when a guy motions and we have to make a coverage check, whether it's, you know, we want to run this stunt, but if this guy does this, it's going to change, we got to feel each other. It's a timing that everybody kind of needs to work Um, and we're working really hard on that and we need to find ways to get more reps. >> Jaylen Wright so cut >> Jaylen Wright, um, I would say Jaylen's doubtful. How did you say >> So now you said what? How prepared do you feel Ali Ali Gordon is to fill that role? >> Prepared. I feel confident. >> Coach, I have a a big picture question for you to kind of get off topic here a little bit, but I'm I'm reading Bill Walsh's Bring Your Own Pencil right now and in it he talks about empowering his coaches to state their claims and coaches and scouts to state their claims in meetings without fear of being proven wrong and reserving the right to change their mind down the road. So the question is, how do you foster an environment that encourages that innovation where guys can speak up without fear of being proven wrong down the road? >> Coaches or players? >> Coaches and scouts. >> Like coaches wanting to bring up their ideas and thoughts? I mean, that's that's what I want. That's what I've always done as an assistant. Um I I don't want a bunch of guys with egos where you know, if you're supposed to be the guy in charge, you're not going to take any ideas from anybody else. Ultimately, all I want to do is win and get better and I hope our coordinators I know our coordinators feel the same way. Um if it's a position coach and his assistant to his position has a good idea, whatever the best idea is, if we think it can work and help our players, let's do it. I mean, for as long as I can remember for calling plays or being a head coach, if if a quality control coach comes to me with a pressure idea and and uh and I think it works and I can figure out how to implement it, I'm going to run it. And then I'm going to give them credit for it if it works and I'm going to take the blame if it doesn't. But at the end of the day, I just I don't care whose idea it is. Um I think that's how you grow and and we're all going to need to do that >> Coach, I got a question about home field advantage. Just in general, as somebody who used to coach at Lambeau, how big a deal is home field advantage? Um what can it do for a team and do other factors such as cold or humidity or altitude are they big factors in the home field advantage? >> Yeah, I think I think all of them are. A lot of guys get used to playing in the environment. Um when we were in Lambeau, a lot of teams weren't used to coming and playing in the cold. Now that we're at home, the heat, people aren't going to be acclimated to the heat. it as far as being at home goes, you know, at certain times you guys have heard it, right? You you got to go on a silent count cuz you can't hear the quarterback's cadence. Well, think about when does it usually get the loudest on a home game? It usually gets the loudest on third down, right? Um when if we're home, our defense is on the field and then what happens is the quarterback's got to get up to the line of scrimmage and he's trying to change a play or he's trying to change the protection or he's trying to call out a different linebacker and then they can't hear him. And you've seen sometimes where it's so loud in the huddle where you can't hear and it makes it very hard it makes it harder for an offense to operate when we can't communicate. Um and and in some environments, it makes it really challenging uh especially in key situations in a game. >> What stands out to you about Steve Spagnuolo defenses? >> Yeah, one I just I I've admired him I've admired him for a long time. I've gotten to know him pretty well. Really when he was back in the Giants, him and I would talk quite a bit. Phenomenal person. Like one of the real good guys in this profession. Just and and I mean that. Like the amount of texts I've gotten from him over the years after a random game, a good one, a hard time, getting this job. I mean he's always one of the first calls. So he's one of the guys that I probably have the most respect for in this profession. Just how he's evolved his defense over the years. It's kind of like you guys were asking me questions about, you know, what what is our defense going to look like 4 weeks from now, 9 weeks from now, 2 years from now. What did it look like my first year in Green Bay versus the second year. He's always evolved. You know, and he's always kind of looked at trends and he's stayed ahead. And and now you see the pressure is all over the place and you see different things that he's been able to do. He just hasn't been the same throughout his whole career. I just can't say enough good things about him and what he's done with that group. >> That's something that ultimately you want to do as well is just constantly change your your defense. >> You have to evolve. You know, you I think you have your core staples and beliefs and I think that always starts with fundamentals and technique, how hard you play, how you run the ball. And especially once you find out what type of players you have and what they can do. You know, there's certain things that I think are really important we're going to stick to until our players do it better, right? But then there's other things that you can pull out from other places that you've been or other things that you've done and and continue to grow. Cuz if you don't, offenses are going to figure you out. >> With with your pass rush, has your philosophy always been that you need it to come primarily from your edge players? And with regard to that, do you need more pass rush, do you think, from your defensive tackles, Seiler, Phillips, Biggers, who obviously does both? >> No, I mean, it hasn't always been it has to come from our edge players. It's always been we need to get it from whoever our best pass rushers are. And I've been in places with really, really good inside guys, where your three technique is one of your leading sack guys, cuz when you have a three technique who can rush, and you can't really chip that guy, and it's harder to get two on him. And then, obviously, I've been in places where your defensive end's the the guy, and so then I've been places where you have to blitz to generate and run a whole bunch of games, and I'm just whatever it takes. >> That was It's kind of a follow-up to Allen's question. When you come up with a game plan, do you game plan against a coach or a specific situation, knowing that Tistan's tendencies disrupted by what you do or his available personnel? >> I mean, I think everything. I mean, when you game plan against somebody, it's it's the coordinator. You You usually you study the coordinator, you know, what are his top plays, what does he like to do, what does he do situationally, what's he doing third down, what's he doing red zone, what's he like on early downs. And then you take it a step further, it's who are their players, right? Cuz ultimately, a lot of times, guys, it's you know, early downs, the calls aren't changing as much as you think. It's It's really who do we have to take away or who do we have to stop? Do they have one really good player that we have to attack and and really pay attention to? Is there a weakness that we really want to go after? Is there a player we have to double over here? Do we have to sell out to stop this running back over here? How are we going to contain the quarterback? It's also match-up issues, right? And then we need to figure out us. Who are they going to attack and who do we need to protect? title: Saints HC Kellen Moore rules two players OUT, talks Raiders' play style, scripted plays + more
text: OK.  Condition of the injured.  We have two players who will miss the game.  Barry Brown— hamstring problem.  Christian Miller— toe injury. Martin Emerson is questionable with a shoulder injury.  All others are available and ready to play. What happened to Nathan Shepherd today? He was okay.  Yes , I trained hard. Of course, I thought we did n't see him today.  And, uh, did Banks have surgery this week? Yes, he had surgery.  Yes, yes, the operation was successful. Of course, uh, everything went well.  And now we'll just stick to the recovery schedule. We'll see how the rehabilitation process goes, but, uh, everything went well. How do you evaluate this week of preparation for the game against the Raiders? What impressed you most about their game and what challenges do you face? Yes, I like the way they play. I think this is a style that everyone probably aspires to.  Their defense works ruthlessly, they constantly press, create chaos on the field with their serve and make important moves at critical moments.  And on offense, they're a physically strong team that focuses on getting the ball out, and they're not afraid to take risks when the opportunity arises— Kirk is always ready to make a pass. You mentioned that the first thing you notice about their game is the effort they put in.  I think we sometimes take it for granted because it's kind of expected, but we saw a lot of high- impact episodes, both individual and team, during the first two weeks. How much does it cost to train?  And to what extent is this inherent in the players themselves? Yes, I think it's a combination.  I believe that effort is a skill. And, you know, I don't think it's a bad thing to focus on effort.  It's a special trait for certain players and teams, and these guys definitely have it.  And, uh, you know, they're doing a great job of not stopping chasing the ball and creating chances. And when situations arise where a pass is needed, it can be difficult to counter them.  And, uh, even in the carry, you can see how physically powerful they are, how their offensive line carries the episodes to the end and how the running backs run.  I think they will demonstrate very powerful football. What have you noticed about how they organize their defense? They seem to be leading the league in defensive efficiency against carryovers right now, and it really stands out. I think it often comes down to them playing very high-quality football, where all eleven players act as one .  They don't make mistakes in the game against takeaways.  They know their responsibilities, and I think that's an important part of stopping the carryover: there's the physical aspect, but there's also the tactical aspect—when everyone understands each other, and I think they do a great job of that. Regarding the two- running back pony setup—is that a situation where you're trying to figure out if that's enough to stay creative throughout the season?  Because it's not something we've seen very often. Yes, there is a time and place for that.  Each week will require different game plans, but I'm sure there 's value in that. Getting both guys on the field, no matter what the running back combination is, I think we can find creative ways to do that going forward. There was a lot of talk about using running backs, load distribution and other things.  How much of this is part of your game plan, and how much depends on the course of events? combination of both factors.  Of course, we have a rough plan of what we want the game to be like.  But sometimes the game goes its own way, and the number of plays, carries, or opportunities can change, simply because we play without a huddle—whoever the running back is, he stays on the field, and we move on. So, the course of the game can be different, which in a way determines the possibilities. Do you have any idea who will replace Berrion, given his absence?  Will it be a team approach?  Like, Yes, yes, we'll take a team approach.  We have a few guys who played there, so we'll see how it goes, but this week, that's exactly what the situation is with Berrion. We hope he returns soon.    Are there any misconceptions about what we mean by game scenarios when it comes to starting combinations?  We're used to thinking about the first 15 draws and everything in that vein.  What does " scripted" actually mean and how do you approach developing that initial game plan? Ultimately, this is just your initial list of plays you are going to use, and throughout the game you always have this list.  I guess it's no different than in the third quarter when you're like, "Hey, these are probably our top five takeaways."  These are our top five passes for this drive." You always try to give players a certain base so they can focus on the main thing.  Of course, there are many situations that determine your next actions, such as third attempts and specific game circumstances. So when we talk about scenario games and the first 15 draws, it's more of a variation or menu of combinations, rather than a rigid algorithm of "this, then this, then this." Yes, that's really a menu. In an ideal world, you build a sequence, hoping that everything will go according to plan, but that does n't always happen. You can find yourself on the right hash line for eight draws in a row, and some of them are designed for the left, so you need to be able to adapt and react to these nuances. You've already started mentioning hash lines, but what exactly does a particular takeaway or "top-5" pass do in such situations? During the opening rallies, you gather information and try to create certain opportunities for your team.  Already during the game, we constantly make adjustments, focus players on a specific plan for the next drive.  Here are the takeaway combinations, here are the passing combinations, here are the possible options for the third attempt.  Again, all this is just to narrow their attention span.

text: What upset me the most about yesterday's game was that I felt like I was watching the New York Giants of 2023, 2024, or 2025 under the leadership of Brian Daboll.  And yes, the situation with rule violations has improved significantly.  I don't think anyone cares about it anymore , but there were so many moments that I couldn't help but ask myself: isn't Brian Daboll standing on the edge?  For example, the combination selection once Dart was eliminated was just awful.  They can neither run with the ball nor pass. Player routes are just chaos.  Jameis Winston, I don't know what happened to his hand, he can't throw the ball.  Maybe he was just having a bad day.  The defense in the secondary is not capable of stopping anything at all.  Devante Adams' 195 yards and two touchdowns —that's [ __ ] embarrassing.  I know Deontay Banks was out, and Parris Campbell was out, and people are going to say, "Oh, well, the defense gave up when Dart left and they saw how bad he played...how bad he was ."  It's not...I know it looked like Brian Daboll's team.  But this isn't Daboll's team, and the players don't act like that, especially on a team led by John Garbo.  They didn't give up.  Javon Holland makes interceptions, knocks out the ball, and causes fumbles on the field.  They did everything they could to get the ball back to the offense, but they just couldn't stop the opponent.  So, the whole match from start to finish was extremely disappointing. Of course, there is nothing worse than injuries. Malik Neighbors goes out on the edge, screaming in pain.  I thought: oh my god, this is too much.  And then Andrew Thomas, Brian Burns.  Then I saw a tweet that Likely and Reese were injured.  I'm like: What the hell is going on here?  And of course, today comes the news that the quarterback is out, possibly for the rest of the season, and we've all been talking about this before.  Just do the surgery now.  If that's what they recommend, then just write this year off.  I know no one wants to do this. I know for a fact that Jackson Dart doesn't want to do this, but at the end of the day, you're focusing on the future, you've got John Garbo for another 4 years, and you've got 2 more years, well, I guess three full years on a rookie contract. So, now we need to think about the future, and if that means having surgery and starting rehabilitation now to be ready for the first week of next year, then so be it .  I hope he will be advised to do exactly that , because, you know, we talked about it here too. If he's out for 6 weeks and the Giants are 0-6 or 1-5 and then he comes back, then all these potential problems will arise again, right?  For example, will everything be the same? How long will it take him to get back on track? Oh, you know, he needs to reestablish rapport with the offense.  Will the Giants be able to play away again? Plus, the offensive line looked terrible.  This is just some kind of disaster.  And in general , no one showed up .    A real nightmare. It was a very painful announcement.  I literally felt like I had been hit in the gut.  I mean, I felt like I was being punched in the gut when I saw him get injured last night. This is just heartbreaking.  I don't want to watch 15 weeks of just bad football again.  Finally, it seemed like we had a team, a real team.  It's like we're talking about the playoffs in December after that Week 1 win with a quarterback who I've proudly said on the show multiple times that he's going to be one of the top five in the league. title: Nick Sirianni on Facing the Chicago Bears
text: Go ahead. >> And Nick, was there any kind of resolution from uh the special teams coordinators talking yesterday about using a tee on kickoffs? >> You know, um obviously with with with that um you know, everything we're doing is within the rules of the game and you know, we'll continue to do the things that we need to do that gives us the best chance to win each and every game um and and that's how we'll proceed as Philadelphia Eagles. >> How do you feel about the urgency this week at practice? >> I'm sorry. >> You know, I think the guys in general had a good week of practice. Um got one more week one more day here. Um that's going to be important part of our process. Guys look good, you know, Zach had a good week. Um tight ends in general had a good week. So, um you know, we'll see where we are at the end of the day. >> You've um uh with Quez Watkins, um there's been some some stuff that like in the backfield, you know, gadgety type plays. Um haven't seen as much of over the middle. Um is that is that an area that you feel like maybe you could focus on a little more with him or is it just like kind of like, you know, guys have a lot of mouths to feed and he's just got to kind of be patient? >> Yeah, you know, again, we want I want individual success for all our guys. Um you know, that individual goals don't happen though without team success first. So, everything we do is going to be to help us give us the best chance to win. Quez is going to be a big part of that um as we continue forward um and cuz we know he's talented. I feel like he's, you know, looking better each week um with, you know, throughout practice um cuz that's your best indicator of what the game's going to look like and you know, of course I'd want him to have 10 catches for 100 yards and Smitty and Quez and you know, whoever um and um but you know, that's just the way the season goes, and we'll see where we are continuing to go. I think, uh, you know, I think Smitty and Tay have had a good start to the season, and there's things that Makai's doing that a stat sheet can't show, and we're pleased with where he's continuing to go, and, you know, his touches will come because he'll be out there because he consistently does the the right thing when it when the ball's not going to him. >> With the guys like with the guys like Zach and Kenny Moore who haven't, you know, gone through a training camp, you know, played football in a while, what kind of things do you look for as far as getting them ramped up within a practice week in order to play? >> Yeah, you're just looking at their movements, seeing how they're moving, how they're feeling after they after practice, and, you know, um, you know, are they learning everything, learning the system, and and, you know, there's habits that the guys that have been here have practiced over and over and over and over again, and you're doing your best job to catch them up on those habits as as fast as you can. Like, whether it's tackling, you know, the way we go about that, the way we go about strip attempts, the way we go about, um, protecting the football, um, and that comes with time. Um, and so, and everything's every situation's a little bit different, and everybody's situation's a little bit different. So, um, you know, I wouldn't say there's a checklist to say, "Hey, this is what we're looking for," but, you know, just asking those questions, uh, to ourselves after every practice, "How did he look? How did he feel?" You know, and asking the player that as well. So, just got a lot of hands on deck to, um, answer those questions, and, like I said, everybody's a little bit different in in in their readiness to go. >> After the game, you had said he can't put into words the responsibility that goes into playing quarterback in the league. Can you put that into words what goes into playing quarterback in this league? >> Yeah, it's it's it's hard work. I'm not sure I can either. Um it's a lot of hard work. It's a lot of responsibility. it's a lot of you know, credit and it's a lot of blame. Um and it it takes great mental toughness to be able to sustain the ups and downs that all these players go through on a weekly basis. And and so um I'm not sure I could put it into words. Uh you know, but there is immense responsibility um you know, to a organization and to a city of playing the most important position in sports. And I'm sure glad we have Jalen Hurts playing uh the most position in sports in Philadelphia because, you know, I love him and everything that he's he's done for us and everything he'll continue to do for us and uh couldn't ask you always say about how we have it couldn't ask for a better partner in this in this and and I feel the same way about Jalen. I couldn't ask for a better partner in this in this journey. >> Sirianni, um how you spent the offseason looking for a new OC and liked what Shawn would bring with a lot of the under center play action stuff. Um if you look at the numbers, you guys are in the lower end of of of having play action. Um is that just a byproduct of the struggles to get the outside zone going and you can't marry it as much with the run or or is you know, like are you surprised that it's it's as low as it is with all the effort that you guys put in to >> Yeah, I you know, I think right now it's a low sample size. We've been doing some some no huddle stuff as well that that you know, sometimes you're running uh different things from from those areas. You know, we always knew there'd be a mix of some of the things that we've done in the past and and some of the new things that we want to bring and you know, I I think that we've had production good production on the ones that we've done. It gives Jalen really good space from the line of scrimmage to the you know, um between him and the line of scrimmage and and I think he's handled those nicely and our our our guys have handled it nicely and and some of that too is being in first and second down and manageable. Um, you know, and not being behind the sticks and we know that we've been behind the sticks a little bit. Um, you know, I think that's a fair question. I think it's just early and early in a sample size and we I'm sure you know, we'll I imagine we'll have this conversation again or not, you know, you know, we'll see where we are at that particular point. Um, I just think it's a little early right now. Um, cuz we're still figuring out who we are and what we do best and all those different things. >> Is Kyler more >> I I know Kyler is still still limited at practice. Is he doing more though than he's done in previous weeks? >> Yeah, he's had a good week. Um, he's had a good week. It's exciting to have him out there. We'll see where we are at the end of the of today. Like I said, that today is a very important part of the process. Um, and I but I feel like he's had a good week. It brings good energy. I've I've really enjoyed I mean, I've I've hated that he hasn't been able to go in uh, for him and for our team, but I've really enjoyed being around him on the sideline and what he's like on a game day. Like he got a lot of knowledge and he's really good with his teammates. Um, and that's been very noticeable, um, uh, to me and and excited when it's the time to get him back out there and and he's worked his butt off to, you know, to be able to get back out there as soon as uh, as soon as possible and I'm excited to have that leadership that I've seen him do when I not playing, you know, while he's playing. So, excited about him and he's had a good week though. >> How do you think uh, >> How Drew and and Drew and Cam looked like with another full week, you know, as center and left guard respectively? >> I think it's always important that when we can, we we have those pads on and so they can work those combinations while also understanding that you got to know and learn how to practice without pads. And and so I think they've done a nice job both those days really taking advantage of the days that that we had the pads on and then also just the communication and all the things and still being able to go through it with without the pads on. So um yeah, they've had a nice week and um you know, we'll see uh we'll see how that pays off. Um but you know, it's it's about the preparation give yourself the best chance to win each week and um you know, it doesn't guarantee anything. It just gives you the best chance and I feel like those two guys at that you know, where they are you know, playing in new spots have um you know, had a good week of of preparation. They got to have another good day today. >> All right.

title: Saquon Barkley & More on Preparing for Chicago Bears
text: But I I tried my best to to go back out there. Um it it didn't go the way I I thought it was going to go. Uh but I mean looking back when I wouldn't change anything on that uh you know we're competitors and I I waited and let it calm down. I feel like I have my strength back. At first I have my strength. So, I got my strength back and, you know, they put me in a position to allow me to go out there after I kind of begged for it. Um, but also told him at the same time that I'm going to protect myself if I feel something. You got my word. But we we we got a a great, you know, from from Tom to all the doctors, everybody, they do a great job. And I'm just happy that they allowed me they trust me enough to go out there. But, you know, I know it made a lot of people upset, but I I wouldn't change that. Um, I I want to be out there and and compete for my team. Sadly, it didn't go the way I would like it. But, um, you know, got a chance to to to go back out there this week. >> How you doing now? I mean, what's this week been like? >> It's been good. Just following the process, following the plan that they have. Um, being super locked into my process and continuing my work. Um big thing is just you know making sure you you know I guess everyone knows what it is sting or um some are worse than others. Uh and just keeping the nerve calm down the inflammation around it. Uh beautiful thing is Monday night game so I have a little more time. Um but right now the mind says I'm I'm good to go. Might have to put on a little cowboy collar for a little bit. Uh, but I rather that than, you know, something with my ankles and my feet and my legs. Uh, >> sore. >> Um, no, I wouldn't say it's sore. It's, you know, when you fire up a nerve, it's pissed off. That's like the best way I could explain it. And you got to do a really good job of calming it down. And, um, feel like they put it put together a great game plan for me. And I just been trying to follow that to the best of my abilities. And, um, I'm excited for another opportunity this week. What's your understanding of whether it can flare up through, you know, football activity or get worse? >> Um, yeah, I mean that was really for a big thing with MRI. Um, make sure I didn't really do anything crazy and anything worse. Um, I've had a history of it before. Uh, this is the first bad one I had in a long time. Um, but it's kind of like football your neck get put in certain certain ways. uh but also like a wakeup call to me. I've been very super active on, you know, focus on like my lower body and my longevity in my career. Um probably wasn't as great as I needed to be with, you know, my neck stability and strengthening my neck. Um so it's like just putting that within my routine. um and having that part of my process and kind of the same way I attack everything from head to toe do the same thing with my neck and um you know go out there and it's good to have MRI knowing that's nothing you know hopefully God willing worry about my career um and I can just go out there and play free and then and try to get you know don't want to say get this thing going because we're two and0 um just keep it rolling um and you know there's obviously some things we want to improve on in offense especially in the rank game. Um, and I'm ready for the opportunity to keep keep getting keep attacking that. >> When when you talk about the run game days, what do you think needs to improve the most? >> Yeah, we just got to um the best way I can answer that just like it's it's not a finished product and don't want it to be a finished product in week two, week three. Um, you want to continue go like this. uh just got to buy in, continue to buy in. We're we're it's all relatively new to all of us. Um in the running game, we're still, you know, as we're learning and trying to continue to buy into something new. You know, we're going out there and we're seeing some some funky looks, some weird looks. You know, it's a sign that the defense still respecting the run game. um which has opened up other things, but it's going to be a beautiful thing. We're in, you know, we're we're all firing at the same page. Um and talking to Jay and the guys about it and talking to O line and it's not like a sense of any panic. Um everybody wants the big numbers, but I'm in a good spot of knowing that the work that's being put in and just continue to focus on our process and the results will come. I wish I could tell you that they were going to come in week one. Um I wish I could guarantee it's gonna come week three. You just never know. But I know that the the results will come and >> when we get this thing rolling, it's going to be it's gonna be something scary. >> You talk about the expectation for those big numbers. Everyone wants I'm sure you want them as well, but this team is still 2 and0. How are you dealing with that balance? Because we we talked about that a lot last season as well. >> It's easy for me. I like winning. I like winning football games. Um yes, I'm the human side of me. Do I like winning football games, rushing for 200 yards? Of course. But I truly don't feel any different from rushing for 200 yards or rushing for 50 yards. Uh each week the the goal is to go out there and find a way to go one and0. And um that's it. That's if you're able to do that. You know, you go back and you're going to have to flush it no matter what. A win or loss, you got to go back and watch film. It's a little easier to to watch the film after a win u rather than a loss. But the goal is to win and whatever it looks like, whatever it takes. Uh that's a a thought that I subscribe to and um I feel like it's been infectious throughout this whole team this season too and we're going to continue to do that. >> Jordan Milatto just talked about how at times he feels like the passing offense is maybe bailing out the offense as a whole. But Jaylen Herz, what have you seen from your quarterback, especially that two-minute drive the last game? >> I mean, he's a he's a dynamic playmaker. Um I think, you know, he he showed that last week, he showed the last two weeks, but he's been showing that his whole career. Um and and that that's the that's the beautiful thing. You know, it's that's only going to get better. The past games are only going to get better and we're going to get the run game going and the way our defense been playing the last however many games. That's what's like there's like a stat that they haven't let up more than 24 points in like however many games, something like that. So, Zach and all those guys and those guys are doing a great job and we we know what the potential is. Um you just can't can't get frustrated with it. You just got to trust it. you got to continue to trust it. Um, and and that, you know, I I'm always going to say when it comes to the run game, that's something I have to own and I'm own that. And yes, the run game is not where we want to be right now, but like I said, the process is there. The the work is being put in. Um, and the results are going to come soon. >> I saw you flexing your left hand on the sideline. How does it affect your your grip and catching the ball? >> I'm a right-hand ball carrier anyway. Um, when I got here, uh, they had to kind of whip me in shape to carry the ball in my left hand. Um, so yeah, when that happened, I wasn't really worried about that part. Um, it's nerve things are scary. Uh, like I said, it's football. It's not the first thing I ever got. It won't be the last. Um, but some are worse than others. And, uh, most important thing we have, our trainers did a really good job of protecting. Sometimes you got to protect yourself. You got, the trainers got to protect you from yourself. And, um, I think they did that. Um cuz I was the second I had any strength back, I was ready to go back out there. Um but I had to wait till my strength fully came back. But my strength is back. We're calming the nerve now and I'm blessed. I get to play Monday night against the Chicago Bears. Uh and I'm excited for that. >> You said you said it was kind of a bad one compared to some of the others you had. Like what was the difference? >> Some hurt a little more than others. Um I won't go into detail about it, but some just hurts a little more than others. Uh, sometimes you get in, you guys would even know unless like the camera catches you going like this. Um, also got to be careful here. I'm not saying like I'm over here getting stingers every game cuz and that puts the medical staff at risk. So, I make sure I clear that up. But, um, um, yeah, it's good. >> Ask this before wearing the collar. How how restrictive how more restrictive is that? >> Yeah. Um the we made a little adjustments to it. Uh you know when I first put it on I really couldn't go like this. I couldn't turn my head and um I was trying to get them know they understood but I was trying to tell them that like your head is like your steering wheel and like for me to run. So when I went out there I actually tried to get into a running back stance and I was like stuck and I had to like try to change my stance. So my stance might look a little different. Go back to kind of how I stood in college a little bit. Anyway, um play around with that. But the restriction part, G and the boys in there did a really good job of combo was something that um not only going to protect me, but also allowed me to uh play the way I want to play, play free. Um I feel like I've been so far put a great week of practice together. And you know, I feel like the process has been really really good and I'm going to stick to that. I'm stick putting, you know, stick to working on the things that I need to work on and the results is going to come as a as a whole in the run game. But at the same time, if we win 17 games and the run games don't get going and we're just winning, you know, I might get some mean comments or you guys might write something bad about me, but at the end of the day, we're winning football games. It's only that matters. >> You don't feel like this will affect you at all on the nose? >> I don't believe I don't think so. Um, no. That's why I'm rehabbing my ass off. Um to get as strong as they need to be. Uh I feel like I'm in a really good spot. Um you know, I know that I know they wouldn't let me go out there if I, you know, wasn't able to do it. Um so I feel like I'm feel I'm in a good spot and just going to let the game come and I'm going to go out there and play fearless. Don't worry about it. Don't worry about re like you know I've dealt with a lot of injuries in my career so you know I battled that the mental side of it a little bit. Um, so I'm excited. I feel good. Feel like I've been having a great practice. Feel like we put a great week of work in as a whole. Um, and we got a great opportunity. >> Couple more. >> What did you think of uh of of Tank and uh and Will? >> I think they did I think they did a great job. Um, I think they did a great job of coming in. It was hard. That was a like that was a hot game. Um, and then last second, you know, those guys having to carry the load a little bit. Um, I think they did a really good job. Did a really good job of running the ball and pass pro. Um, in that two-minute drive, Will did some really great stuff that no one's going to write about, no one's going to know about, but uh only onlybody that's really going to give him credit, someone the guys in the RV room. So, um, think did a really good job on the touchdown run, the run before that, sending it to him, never going down. Uh, it's it's going to take all of us. It's going to take all all of us um as a group to get this thing going, especially with the offensive line um and the tight ends and the wide series. But like I said, I'm not going to say, oh, keep sitting here saying we're close, we're close. I'm just going to say the the process is where it need to be. He's like, "Ah, we we're just, you know, if we if we just put our hat front side here or had our hand placement more down the middle, not really on the back side of a shoulder pad pad." It's not as simple as knots and crosses. It's not. And, um, you know, you got to win. You got to win. You're down. And it's not just the, you know, first second down. What is your communication style like with him? >> Put on my jacket. >> Uh still growing a little bit. I mean, uh, every day I I got to prove to myself that I'm the player that I say I am and how great I am. Um, other than that, shoot, I just, you know, hope that the people that looks on the outside end that they see the same thing. I mean, either way it go, I still got to play. I still got to be great. I still got to come out here and do my 111. But it's pretty dope to, you know, have everybody else that is here in the city, the fans, the media, they get to see me get better, you know, throughout the season, each week. >> Big match up for this team. Monday Night Football, Chicago, Soldier Field, it doesn't get much bigger than that. What are your expectations for this game? >> Uh, honestly, just go out there and have fun. I mean, we got to stop the run. That's one of the main things, but other than that, uh, continue to play as one. everybody continue to use they, you know, play their 111 and uh it's going to be exciting, man. It's a nice prime time game versus a a playoff type opponent. So, this is one of those games we need and I felt like to go where we're going, we got to play games like this. So now I'm being big fighter.

title: Jalen Hurts on Preparing for the Chicago Bears
text: How are you doing?  Say it again.  It's great that he's back.  The history he has here, the experience he has. I know it's important to him.  I know he's been wanting to come here for a long time , and it's good to compete with him again.  Just a player with high intelligence.  You know , great hands, knows how to break away from defense.  He has been very consistent throughout his career. How do you think you do so well on your third attempt at the start of the season?  I don't know.  It's hard to say for sure. We just find a way to implement these attempts.  You know, often you don't want to find yourself in such situations, but we manage to find a way out.    Is there anything special about the way Sean McVay uses the pace of the game? Special? Yes.    I can't say.  I can't say. So what do you think about how you've been using it so far? Ahem.  I mean, throughout my career, everyone has had a different approach, so I would say the word " different" is better than "special ," it's a whole puzzle that the coach puts together.  It's a whole element, a whole whole puzzle in everything we do, so it's not one component of our offense that drives the game.  It's the ability to do everything based on what I know and the conversations I had with the coach.  So, you know, it all depends on his leadership, on how he feels about the game, how he wants to build it, and how he understands who we become as we form our identities. You talked about winning tendencies, and he said that during the game you understand what exactly is required of you .  What influences this?  How do you even come to this ? Ahem.  I think it comes with maturity, experience, reflection on those experiences, and, you know, some of the scars that I have.  It, you know, puts me in a position to, you know, try to do what needs to be done, communicate, be on the same page, find clarity and coherence when going out on the field to complete tasks. But, in the end, it all comes down to poise, focus, the will to win, and determination.  And, um, going out there and, you know, giving it your all, being dedicated to the cause.    The example you gave is, uh, the Chicago game in '22.  I know it was disappointing in that game, but if you think back to that day, what do you remember about your game and how you realized it was a win? Ahem.  That game, uh.  It was a game where.  I think we made some losses early in the game.    They moved the ball well.  We didn't use all the possibilities.  The game was much more difficult than we wanted.  Um, after all, you know, the league exists to win.  That's the point.  Everyone made an effort for this .  And I think that's a great thing— being in my position and having different coaches every year, that's one of the advantages. Seeing how everyone has their own approach to the same goal.  So to sum it up, you know.  What difference does it make how it's done? You know, the main thing is to find a way to win.  And make sure we're all on the same page. I think that's part of my mentality throughout the game.  And, you know, I think one thing that I really appreciate about everything that we've had is the progression throughout the week, the learning process, the absorption of information, and the more disciplined schedule to be able to work on mistakes throughout the week and fix them so that by game day I'm confident in what I want to do.  I have clarity on what Coach Shen sees.  Um, and more.  I think it's also important to understand that continuity is built when you experience certain things together.  So I think it was really good for us to win these last two games, these, you know, these first two games of the year, given the nature of the game and where we are right now in terms of working relationships and dynamics.  Um, you know, we're excited about what we believe we're capable of, but at the end of the day, all you have is a job.  You have no promises, you can't do anything else.  So, you know, we just work, talk, strive to improve, seek mutual understanding, and I try to learn everything I can, you know.  I always try to be like a sponge, absorb as much information as possible, and eventually I will find a way.    Do you still like this process? Yes, I like it. I think, um, you know, the game started to slow down because of experience, not because I was doing it this way because of this coach.  Not through heredity, but through experience. You mentioned that you don't necessarily care how it looks, as long as it's done.  I guess when do you think there was a moment in your career when you felt like it became clear?    I can't say.  I don't want to get off topic, you know, um, out of respect.  You know, we have a very strong opponent coming to us this week. Let's focus on that, but all of this experience is valuable. Every experience, you know, I've said this many times.  Every experience is valuable.  Um, and we have a very strong opponent who caused us problems last year.  So, I think we've collectively analyzed it and are trying to give it our all on Monday. Will you be able to rely on Darius Cooper as much as you did at the end of last week's game? Just talk about his progression, you know, from when he came here as an undrafted free agent to where he is now. Yeah, you know, it's, um, I don't think it's a surprise what kind of player he is and how he presents himself.  Um, his character and how he works.  He, he is always ready to prove himself and do everything to help the team be in the best position .  So I'm proud of him and happy to see his professional growth .  You know, he's...sometimes you forget how young he is in his career, but he's, you know, he's going to be a great player. What stands out in the video of this week's Bears game? Um, they, they're flying towards the ball.  They fly towards the ball.  I think it all starts with Coach Allen.  He, he always did a great job wherever he was.  And you know, they, they have a knack for playing with the ball for a long time.  That's what's inherent in their defensive coordinator.  So, keeping in mind, uh, keeping in mind all the different options that we're going to get from them, and, you know, I think for us, on our end, and Shannon confirmed this, we try to stick to the schedule, and everyone has to do their part, do what they're asked to do on each individual play.  To go out on the field and just keep developing. You mentioned on Sunday that teamwork is very important, not only for the offensive line, but for all offensive players.  Second week with Drew Brees, how was it Yes.  I mean, everything will be fine.  You know, this is not a game where you can make any promises.  It all depends on the work.    It all depends on the time you put into it.  So I repeating this because it applies to Drew, it applies to Cam, Coach Sean, and every guy who gets new opportunities.  This applies to us too, because we are implementing a new attack pattern, right?  It's work, it's time invested, and we continue to work on it. You mentioned several times about continuity and collaborative learning over the course of several weeks.  I think it happens differently with everyone, but with Te developed this harmony so quickly.  Why do you think it developed so quickly? I think Te thinks less because it's something he's familiar with.  That's part of the deal.  And secondly, it's the time we spent together, learning about each other.    The opportunities I had to study his body language and understand what kind of player he was.  So everything I've seen up to this point gives me complete confidence.  And, want to continue to grow.  We believe that the goal overall, regardless of individual players, as a team, as a collective—is to make this something special, ours.  So I don't think we've seen that result yet, but we just want to grow. Jaylen, you've often talked about understanding and learning the history of quarterbacks here in Philadelphia.  Do you do this in relation to the historic venues where you play, like Lambeau or, in this case, Soldier Field ?  Do you look at it and think, "Damn, real legends played here." I have moments, and, you know, last week for me was...it was, really, a great feeling.  And it's a little emotional, you know, driving up to the stadium and seeing Steve McNair on the banner outside.  Ahem.  He was one of those—he was the only one I looked up to.  Ahem.  Yeah, I was able to meet, you know, Michael Jordan and build a relationship with him, with Tom Brady and the other guys. But I wouldn't call Steve McNair the only one I really looked up to, watched, and, you know , admired— even though I never got to meet him.  So I think that win was special for that reason, and I was reminded of that when we pulled up to the stadium , and it really hit home for me.  So, um...I don't know if this answers your question, but it's an example of the history of the game and how you, as a player, tie yourself to the examples before you, to the pioneers, so that you can forge your own path. What exactly about McNair fascinated you so much? All.  Ahem.  I can talk for a long time about his abilities and his manner of behavior.  Ahem. And it all came from his style.  It was something no one expected.  Um, it was just, you know, a little ahead of its time. And so, you know, there's a lot of history at that position, and I was a black quarterback, the history of quarterbacks in Philadelphia.  I think he's following in the footsteps of those great players who were here, and with some of the obstacles he had to overcome, and the example he set.  So, you know , I think, in terms of versatility and ability, I was on a par with Vince Young.  Later I learned that Vince Young, as a child, I didn't know, looked like Steve McNair, but, you know, there are great examples around.  And um... you know, we're all still kids.  So that was a special moment for me. Thank you, Ele.

title: Nick Sirianni on Preparing For the Chicago Bears
text: I don't. The Bears. Yeah, I know. What what what do they do well and does it complicate things when you don't know who's going to be playing quarterback? >> Yeah, you know, I I think they're they got some great players all around. Some really really good players and then we're I think the coaching's outstanding. You know, coach Johnson, coach Allen, coach Hightower all do a phenomenal job. And if they've done a phenomenal job through this league through the past, you know, decade. So a lot of respect for them and how they play. Yeah, you know, you go into each game and you're thinking, you know, who's the quarterback? How do you affect them? All those different things and every quarterback's a little bit different. But you do what you do best and and you go there, but yeah, it gives you a couple more layers to think through, but you know, that's that's life in the NFL, right? There's always there's always a guy that could play or couldn't play each and every week, right? In every position and every coordinator has to plan accordingly. And so that's that's not new for us and you know, we'll go through our process like we always do in that >> Sorry. >> Um >> Last year after maybe you guys ripped his shirt off in the off season, he said some things that were pretty bold, pretty brash. You yourself can be emotional. How do you balance as a coach? Thank you. How do you balance as a coach being authentic, being who you are and maybe I don't know crossing the line would be the right phrase necessarily, but acting in a way that may have people going, "Hmm." >> I think the last thing that you can worry about as a head coach is trying to please anybody outside your building. And and in in which case too, it's you you got to always do you always got to be yourself. You always got to do it within the rules. I tell our guys that all the time. Be yourself, have fun, enjoy this, you know, and do it within the rules. Um and you can't worry about pleasing anybody outside the building. There's because regardless of what you do, if you're emotional if you take your shirt off, if you don't take your shirt off, if you're emotional, if you're not emotional, some of the people are going to say, "Man, I like that." And some are going to be like, "Man, I don't like that." That's leadership. That's what it is. So, your your job is to be yourself and do everything you can do as a head coach um to get your team ready to play and get your team better on a daily basis. Um and you can't look at the outside to see how you you can please because it it's a it's a impossible task. >> Then tell us how much >> Just win games. >> Right? >> How much of a challenge is their running game and what are your thoughts so far on your run defense? >> Yeah, they obviously uh provide a lot of different uh things in the run game that are challenging. Um you know, I I guess I got a lot of respect for their coaching and and how they go about it and obviously their players, you know, I think Wright's a really good player. Um DeAndre's playing really good. I really enjoyed being around DeAndre for the year that he was here and you know, he has this a great ability to have these one cuts if you over play him, have these one cuts to be able to make him a miss um if you over pursue. Um you know, and so uh again, just got a a lot of respect for that the way they go about it. Um and and and the problems that they can provide. You know, we got to play with great fundamentals. We got to play with great discipline um within that. Um it's always going to be about block destruction and blocking it for the O-line, D-line and and those are going to be critical this week. Um and you know, it's a process, right? It's a process this of getting your run defense, your pass offense, whatever it may be, run offense, pass defense um to where you want it to go. And so, we you know, we're I feel like we're making steps. There's a reason that we're in pads, you know, once a week until the, you know, and because the league rules allow you once a week and then, you know, later on in the season there's not uh you're not able to every week, but there's a reason we're going to be in pads every every Wednesday, you know, unless it's a significant week where it's a short week, um, because that's how you get better at block destruction and blocking, you know, and this is a big day for us today of of working our block destructions when we have our pads on and you still got to to be able to do that with your pads off as well, but this is a really unique day for us to be able to to a unique day. This is a very important day for us to be able to do those work those things to continue to get better at what we need to. >> What's it like having Zach Ertz back and and how do you see him fitting in and if he's going to be ready to play on Sunday night? >> Yeah, we we haven't practiced yet, obviously, as you guys know and, you know, we'll go out there today. Um, like with every player, you know, trust is built through practice and through reps. So, you know, we'll see where he is. Uh you know, I know, um, you know, I've seen Zach plenty of times and, you know, this will be new for Sean and and Ryan uh of seeing him go to work. So, you know, we'll go out practice today, see where he is and and see how we we need to play this thing out, but I'm excited to have Zach on the roster and and moving and moving forward. >> What do you see right now in his understanding of the system where you guys are 2 weeks into it and what he can do in the offense? >> Who's that, Zach? >> Yeah. >> Yeah, you know, I haven't quizzed him yet on anything. Um, we'll go out there, you know, as far as like, "Hey, what do you what do you you know, we'll go out there today, see if how he lines up and, you know, as far as the knowledge of the system, there's a lot of plays that are similar throughout the NFL. Um, in offenses, um, it's just about getting, you know, you're speaking one language and then now it's about speaking another language, right? You're speaking English, now you got to speak French or whatever it may be and and uh you know, so now it's a little easier in a game plan week. Um you learn the origins of where all the words come from. Um and then you don't have quite the whole playbook to have to learn. And so we'll see where he is. I guess it's too early to say in my mind like you know, where he is, but we'll I we will quiz him and figure out where you know, on on different things, but you also see do that in practice and walk through of how he's coming out of the huddle and everything like that. >> I know you're at practice in a little bit, but with Saquon Barkley, any update on that? Is there any long-term concern? Practice today? >> Uh yeah, we'll get you guys injury report. Um you know, I know Saquon does everything he can do to get himself ready to play each and every week. Um love that about him and his work ethic and we'll see what see where we are. >> You've spoken highly about Kenny Moore in the past. What's your your your background with him? And is he someone who can play safety though he has really done >> Yeah, I think the world of uh Kenny Moore. Um you know, he is a really good football player, really good person, um great teammate, um you know, and so being able to add him to our team uh is a big deal. Um and I'm pumped about that and you know, I was able to spend 3 years with him. Highly competitive. Um you know, being the offensive coordinator and not the head coach at you know, at that time um you know, you get I could see the battles that he had with with our receivers and in different scenarios. So I love his competitiveness. Um him and Zach Pascal would go at it and on a lot of block destruction things within practice. Another former Eagle. So um yeah, and you get around guys like that that you've you you you know, it's it's a no-brainer when you're when you when Howie came to me and asked me what what I thought of the guy and then obviously watched the tape. I I got to watch a little bit of the tape and um and then hey, what do you think of the guy? And you know, it was everybody said the same thing. I obviously have had some Indy guys here in the past and uh currently and everyone's report of what they said all matched up and it's no surprise because everybody at in that at you know, his old place really thought the world of him because of who he is on a daily basis consistently. Yeah, we'll see. Um we'll see, you know, I think that he has ability to to be versatile um which is really important. Um you know, especially with guys, you know, that are you know, backing up and everything like that. So, we'll see where he is. We got to get some reps um and those things get answered within practice. Um and with reps. So, uh today is an important day for many reasons. Obviously with that with that as well. >> Nick, why do you think you guys don't have a takeaway yet? >> I'm sorry. >> Why do you think you guys don't have a takeaway yet? >> Um you know, sometimes those those come in bunches. Um you know, we we work like crazy on it. I wouldn't say that we've had a ball that I felt like we dropped um as far as an interception goes. Um you know, I think that the quarterback, you know, we've had a couple scrambles by quarterbacks with against quarterbacks that are good at getting out of the uh getting out of the pocket um with our first two opponents. So, you haven't had a couple of those strip sack fumbles that you get sometimes in those scenarios. you know, our job well, I always want our team you get more tackling attempts than you do takeaway attempts in a game. So, you bet your your tackling fundamentals come first, always. Um And so, and you don't want to put the tackle at at risk by going after a strip attempt. Um and so, you know, some games we chart it every week. Hey, here's how many strip attempts opportunities were. Here's how many times we took it a attempt at it. You can't score points unless you shoot the ball. Um but you never want and those those are judged by us as far as when we tell them to take these strip attempts, but you never sacrifice the tackle in which case. So, it's just some of them's been attempts and as far as I think we've done a good job of taking attempts that were there. There just hasn't been as many and and you guys would kind of be surprised of how little there actually are in a certain game. And what that's why it's so important that when you have those opportunities, when it's a strip attempt opportunity, you take advantage of that. But we've had some good attempts at it and they've done had some good ball security there and you know, we just got to keep going through our process. I know we drill it. I know we it like unlike anybody at really at the end of the day and we talk about it. Um and so we just got to stick to the process and I think you know, that's such a key. Can you stick to the process when you're not producing results? Can you stick to what you know is going to get the ball out when the results aren't there yet? And that's a key in not just takeaways, but everything. Can you stick to that thing um knowing that the work's going to be what what gets the ball out when you have those opportunities in the game. >> When Skyler's went on IR, was there like a contingency plan as Skyler's led to Zach Ertz knowing Dallas Goedert's injury history or what he might do in a game like this? >> Um you discuss everything as you as you go through things. Um you know, I don't think you look at anything and say, "Hey, this guy could you just let it play out." Um and so you know, everything's discussed. Everything has a plan. That's what you know, you appreciate so much about Howie. Uh that's what I appreciate so much about Howie is everything's thought out. Everything's got a plan. Um and you know, here we are uh today in in the situation we're in and and Zach being here that, you know, I'm excited about that opportunity for him. >> Do a couple more. >> Given uh given how the last game against the Bears went, what's your approach this week in terms of are you are you emphasizing that point? Like how it went on the ground and maybe from a physicality perspective or or not? >> Yeah, you know, again, each week brings different keys to victory um both offensively, defensively, special teams-wise. Um, and so, um you know, there's there's unique things each week based off of the opponent that you're playing. Um, we never really get into revenge. I think I've talked to you guys about that like in the sense of that last about a minute and then um your habits and your fundamentals take over. And so, you know, this is a 2026 Eagles versus 2026 um Bears and, you know, both both teams going to be a battle. Both teams are good good football teams. And, you know, this week's going to be about the same thing every you know, hey, what is what does it take to win this week? You know, there's going to be certain things, but then there's always common things, you know, we got to win the turnover battle. We got to win the explosive play battle. We have to play with great fundamentals. Those are keys each and every There's keys for one game and then there's keys that that are your general keys, you know, week in week out. And those are the things, you know, that are consistent throughout the year um as playing with good fundamentals, playing with good effort, playing together, all those different things. >> Look at the two backup running backs. Why do you like the committee approach there and what do you like about those two guys? >> Uh Tank and Will, you're saying? Yeah, yeah, you know, I think they both bring a unique skill set. We trust the heck out of both of them. Um, they've both made play or Tank made a great tackle on special teams uh in the game. Will Will's made plenty of tackle uh tackles on special teams. Um, I think it's just trust. You know, you trust those guys and and they both have earned reps and they both you know, have different things that they bring to the table. It's kind of like the same thing with a receiver. Why why throw this guy this one and this guy that one, you know, you know, not to say they both can't do different things, but they both have different skill sets that you try to utilize um within a game. And so, um yeah, I mean, obviously that proved to be uh majorly uh helpful this week um to have backs that we, you know, the backups that we have um when Saquon was not able to continue to go. And um yeah, I love that that room and I love the depth of that room and I love the closeness of that room, that, you know, and yeah, it's just a good solid running back room. >> Last one. Was there a time when you saw something from Dontayvion Wicks where you thought we might have a steal here? >> Yeah, I think that that happens when you're watching the tape prior to him even getting here. I think that's why, you know, howie was aggressive to go and get him because we saw the potential of what he could be and then we knew about the person with the guys that were in Green Bay. And so, you know, when he started doing the things that we saw on tape, it wasn't a surprise because, you know, there was a lot of work that went into identifying that. Um and you know, the words that were being said by Sean and Ryan were matching what we saw on tape. Um and yeah, he's he's been a great addition. Um love his I love the way I love his physicality within the game of football and his mentality and competitiveness for football. Forget about how explosive he is at the top of the route, his ability to to catch contested balls. I just love his mentality of how he goes about his daily work and the and the competitiveness that happens on the field with him. >> All right. Thanks for it. >> Thanks, you.

title: Press Conference: Nick Sirianni
text: Go ahead. >> And Nick, was there any kind of resolution from the special teams coordinators talking yesterday about using a TE on on kickoffs? you know, um obviously with with with that um you know, everything we're doing is within the rules of the game and you know, we'll continue to do the things that we need to do that gives us the best chance to win each and every game. Um and and that's how we'll proceed as Philadelphia Eagles. >> How do you feel about interception this week of practice? >> I'm sorry. >> How do you feel about this week of practice? >> You know, I think the guys in general had a good week of practice. Um got one more week, one more day here. Um that's going to be important part of our process. Guys look good. You know, Zach had a good week. Um tight ends in general had a good week. So um you know, we'll see where we are at the end of the day. >> You've um uh with Mai Lemon. Um there's been some some stuff that like in the back field, you know, gadgety type plays. Um haven't seen as much of over the middle. Um, is that is that an area that you feel like maybe you could focus on a little more with him or is it just like kind of like, you know, guys have a lot of mouths to feed and you just kind of got to be patient? >> Yeah, you know, again, we want I want individual success for all our guys. Um, you know, that individual goals don't happen though without team success first. So, everything we do is going to be to help us give us the best chance to win. Um, Mai is going to be a big part of that um, as we continue forward. Um, and because we know he's talented, I feel like he's, you know, looking better each week, um, with, you know, throughout practice. Um, because that's your best indicator of what the game's going to look like. And, you know, of course, I'd want him to have 10 catches for 100 yards and Smitty and Tay and, you know, whoever. Um, and, um, but, you know, that's just the way the season goes and we'll see where we are continue to go. I think uh you know I think Smitty and Tay have had a good start to the season and there's things that Mai is doing that a stat sheet can't show and we're pleased with where he's continuing to go and you know his touches will come because he'll be out there because he consistently does the the right thing when it when the ball's not going to him >> with guys like with guys like Zack and Kenny Moore who haven't you know gone through a training camp you know played football a while. What kind of things do you look for as far as getting them ramped up within a practice week in order to play? >> Yeah, you're just looking at their movement, seeing how they're moving, how they're feeling after the after practice. And you know, um, you know, are they learning everything and learning the system and and you know, there's habits that the guys that have been here have practiced over and over and over and over again. And you're doing your best job to catch them up on those habits as as fast as you can. Like whether it's tackling, you know, the way we go about that, the way we go about strip attempts, the way we go about um protecting the football. Um, and that comes with time. Um, and so and everything's every situation's a little bit different and everybody's situation's a little bit different. So, um, you know, I wouldn't say there's a checklist to say, hey, this is what we're looking for, but you know, just asking those questions, uh, to ourselves after every practice. How did he look? How do he feel? You know, and asking the player that as well. So, just got a lot of hands on deck to, um, answer those questions. And like I said, everybody's a little bit different in in in their readiness to go. >> After the game, Jay said he can't put into words the responsibility that goes into playing quarterback in the league. Can you put that into the words what goes into playing quarterback in this league? >> Yeah, it's it's it's hard work. I'm not sure I can either. Um it's a lot of hard work. It's a lot of responsibility. Um it's a lot of, you know, credit and it's a lot of blame. Um, and it it takes great mental toughness to be able to sustain the ups and downs that all these players go through on a weekly basis. and and so um I'm not sure I could put it into words uh you know but there is immense responsibility um you know to a organization and to a city of playing the most important position in sports and I'm sure glad we have Jaylen Herds playing uh the most position at sports in Philadelphia because you know I love him and everything that he's he's done for us and everything he'll continue to do for us and uh couldn't ask I always say about how we I couldn't ask for a better partner in this in this and and I feel the same way about Jaylen. I couldn't ask for a better partner in this in this journey. >> Sitting um how you spent the offseason looking for a new OC and liked what Shawn would bring with a lot of the under center play action stuff. Um if you look at the numbers you guys are the lower end of of of having play action. Um, is that just a byproduct of the struggles to get the outside zone going and you can't marry it as much with the run or or is you know like are you surprised that it's it's as low as it is all the effort that you guys put in to >> Yeah, you know, I think right now it's a low sample size. We've been doing some some no huddle stuff as well that that you know sometimes you're running uh different things from from those areas. I mean, they've been able to run the ball around at will.  They were able to protect the pass.  They have the benefit of having those two pillars, Jordan Mailata and Lane Johnson.  What we saw last week was what happens when some of those pieces move on the inside, and I was struck by how the Tennessee Titans tried to disorient those players and cause confusion.  One thing they did was execute many tactical plays.  They used some split formations.  Obviously, they have Jeffery Simmons, who is one of the best interior linemen. He's a beast, everyone, in case you didn't know.  It's incredible.  I always hated playing against him. So, they place these guys at different levels.  And what I mean by different levels is that, usually, you're going to pretend you're my offensive player, you're going to be my right tackle. I'm going to be the right guard. So, the only reason I do this on the right side is because, you know, it's just natural for me to go to the right side.  So, if we have a technique three and we have a defensive end, that means defensive tackle, defensive end, you and I can think of this as a two-on-two block.  You and I are responsible for these two types.  Now, if the formation gets weird, if there are two guys outside of you, if there's a guy here and a linebacker approaching the line of scrimmage, then it can become a three-on-two. Then it can become, let's make these offensive linemen spread out, because when we're together, we're strong.  But when they make you go that way and this defensive tackle makes me go this way, and we have another guy circling from the other side, there's a gap in the line of scrimmage.  There are gaps, and when you don't have these repetitions together like that interior part of the Philadelphia Eagles' offensive line, it shows.  Although I'm not worried, because those things get fixed with repetition.  So, if you're an Eagles fan, don't panic. What worries me is, why was Saquon wearing Howie Long's cowboy collar?  Well, that looked weird.  They were checking his shoulder over there.  I've had nerve cramps before.  That makes that arm go a little quieter.  So, we need to keep an eye on Saquon Barkley and his ability to stay in the lineup.
